title: Play the M4 gate and write m4-evaluation.md
description:
Play the M4 gate and write `docs/milestones/m4-evaluation.md`.

**Can you lose a delve, and does losing it sting?**

Stated as something to feel rather than to measure, in the same spirit as M0's. §9: "you should be
able to stand in front of a door at 5 hit points and genuinely not know whether to open it. If you
can, the loop exists. If you cannot, no amount of narration quality substitutes."

Every prior milestone has one of these and they are the most valuable documents in the repo —
`m3-evaluation.md` §8 is what made M4 plannable at all. The workflow M2 built and M3 used applies:
every session writes itself to `server/sessions/`, so when something goes wrong in play the file
that proves it is already on disk. Copy the session worth keeping into `docs/evidence/` and, if it
earns it, into the suite as a replayed fixture.

What this gate has to answer that the others did not:

- Whether attrition actually bites, or whether the numbers make the door decision a formality in
  either direction.
- Whether the clock is felt. It is deliberately diegetic and unlabelled — the shrinking light, and
  signs for the alert clock. If the player never noticed a clock was running, that is the finding.
- Whether losing stings when nothing persists. The sting is meant to come from within the session:
  what was spent, how far you got, what you left behind. This is the assumption the milestone rests
  on and it may not hold — and if it does not, that is a better finding than a pass.
- Whether the DM's improvisation and the board agree more often than they did. Risk 3 is the one
  M4 attacks from two sides, with the engine-owned objective and with markers.

Carry forward what did not get exercised, the way M3 did with the room-qualified `PropRef`.
acceptance_criteria: A played session, its log copied into docs/evidence/, and docs/milestones/m4-evaluation.md with a verdict on the gate question and a section 8 listing what M4 hands forward. Findings that were not exercised are named as such.

title: What the projection carries about hurt, clocks and the objective
description:
## Question

What does the world-state projection carry into the DM prompt about hurt, clocks, the objective and
consumables — and in what form?

§15 names this as the expensive part of M4: "the projection work that carries hurt, clock and
objective state across a room boundary as fiction, which is the same problem M3 is already inside."
Nothing else in the epic owns it.

## Where it lives

`DmService.java:842` and around it. The projection is a hand-built markdown block: `## The fight`,
`## Momentum`, `## Established`, `## Ways out`, `## Grid`. It never truncates (that is the whole
point of it against the 6-turn transcript window), so anything added here is in every prompt for
the rest of the session.

## The precedents disagree, and that is the question

- `## Momentum` ships a **count**: "2 checks have failed in a row." A bare number, deliberately
  labelled as a block rather than a sentence because the model read a trailing sentence aloud.
- `## The fight` **forbids** counts: "never state the order, the round number, or anyone's hit
  points. Those are on screen." `dm.md` forbids reading hit points aloud, and `AGENTS.md` combat
  narration says a wound is described, not counted — "handing the model a fraction is an invitation
  to read it."

So: does a filling light clock arrive as `4/6`, or as "the lantern is guttering"? Does hurt arrive
as `5/12`, or as "badly hurt"? The two blocks in the same file answer differently and both have
reasons behind them.

## `## Ways out` is the cautionary tale, and it is recent

The block listed doors and said nothing about their state. The model re-improvised the answer every
turn; both 2026-09-07 sessions invented an ATHLETICS DC 20 to kick a door that was never shut, and
one spent two turns on a key against a lock that does not exist. The fix was the prompt telling the
truth. **A projection block that is vague about state is worse than no block**, because the model
will fill the gap and be consistent about the wrong thing.

## What has to be decided

- Hurt: counted or described, and if described, what the bands are and who owns them.
- Clocks: which clocks appear, in what form, and whether a clock the player cannot see (ALERT) is
  described differently from one they can (LIGHT).
- The objective: carried or not carried, and what stops the narrator inventing a second one.
- Consumables: counts, and how the block makes "you have no potions" something the model will not
  narrate around. §9 is blunt that the model always says yes.
- Whether any of this belongs in `dm.md` and `dm-tools.md` instead of, or as well as, the
  projection. `AGENTS.md` records that prompt and parser must agree, and that terse instructions
  win on length — measure before believing an edit helped.

## Watch for

The Established block already leaks grid coordinates (emberdelve-pa8, and m2-evaluation §8). Adding
blocks is adding surfaces for that. Nothing in this projection may produce a number the narrator
would read aloud.
acceptance_criteria: A decision, recorded as a resolution comment, on what hurt, clock, objective and consumable state reaches the DM prompt and in what form — counted or described, in which block, with the wording. No number that a narrator would read aloud.
close_reason: Resolved: one always-present ## The party block; bands not fractions, except counts that drive a tool decision. Full answer in the resolution comment.

comments.text:
# Resolution — 2026-09-09

Hurt, clocks, the objective and consumables reach the DM prompt as **one always-present
`## The party` block**, in **bands, not fractions**, with the counts that drive a tool
decision left as counts.

## The rule that decides all of it

**A count that drives a tool decision stays a count. A count that only describes state
becomes a band.**

This is the reconciliation the ticket asked for, and it explains both precedents rather
than picking a winner between them. `## Momentum`'s "2 checks have failed in a row" is the
input to `dm-tools.md`'s two-failure escalation rule, so it stays a number — and
emberdelve-vy7 is the evidence, because both 2026-09-07 sessions escalated on the *first*
failure and a band there ("things have been going badly") is exactly the vagueness that
made turn-1 escalation a coin flip. `## The fight`'s ban on hit points stands for the
opposite reason: no tool takes hit points as an argument. None of the seven does. The
mechanics model decides *whether* to roll, never how much damage, so the fraction buys
nothing and costs what AGENTS.md warns about — "handing the model a fraction is an
invitation to read it."

The rule also predicts the answer for anything added later, which is the point of writing
it down rather than listing four decisions.

## What the code does today, which is not what anyone intended

`DmService.java:797` ships **every entity as `5/12 hp`**, every turn, in both prompts. So
the ticket's question — 5/12 or "badly hurt" — is already answered as 5/12 *by accident*,
against AGENTS.md and against `BeatRenderer.condition()`, which sits twelve files away with
four bands and a comment explaining why a fraction in a beat is an invitation to read one.
Two mechanisms in one codebase disagreeing. That fraction goes.

## Hurt

Bands, from **one shared source** — `BeatRenderer.condition()`'s existing four, extracted so
there is one wound vocabulary in the system rather than two:

    > 0.7  barely marked
    > 0.4  bloodied
    > 0.15 badly hurt
    else   barely standing

Not a second set of thresholds for the projection. A creature described one way in a combat
beat and another way in the block above it is the copper-key failure in miniature.

The number the player needs is on their own hit point bar. The DM never needed it.

## Whose hurt, and where

The party gets **its own block**, `## The party`, above `## Entities present`.

Today the party member sits *inside* `## Entities present`, marked `[the player]`. After
emberdelve-4h9.1 that list holds two different lifetimes: party state is session-scoped and
survives a room boundary, hostiles are rebuilt from room content. The block that has to
survive a crossing should not be the one that gets rebuilt. Invariant 2 also applies —
`List<PartyMember>`, so the block is a list, not a line about the player.

It gives the clocks, the consumables and the objective somewhere coherent to sit: all three
are party facts, not room facts, which is why none of them fits in any block that exists.

## The block, as wording

```markdown
## The party

Session state. It followed them in here and it will follow them out.

- `roderick` — Roderick, badly hurt, at (6,1)
- objective: not yet found
- lantern: guttering
- potions: 0 · torches: 1 · rope: 0

There is nothing else here worth carrying out. Do not invent a second.

The lantern and anything moving toward the party are the engine's to change, not yours.
Narrate what you are told has happened. Do not decide that the light goes out.
```

Grid coordinates stay on the party line: `move_entity` needs bounds and adjacency, `## Grid`
exists to make them mean something, and `dm.md:47` already forbids saying one aloud. Dropping
them here while every prop keeps its own would break "what is near what" — emberdelve-pa8 is
about facts leaking coordinates into `## Established`, which is a different surface.

## Clocks

**Both LIGHT and ALERT, as bands, with a fact-not-cue line.**

ALERT has to be in the projection even though the player cannot see it, or honest
foreshadowing is impossible — that was already settled at charting ("the projection lets the
DM foreshadow the alert clock honestly"). LIGHT has to be there or the narrator writes a
steady lantern while the radius shrinks on screen.

The fact-not-cue line is load-bearing and it is not boilerplate. The `## Secrets` block
proves this exact model narrates a thing into being when a block reads as a promise: told a
goblin "will come out fighting", the prose model wrote it climbing out — lid grinding, hand
on the rim — on a turn where nothing had spawned and no fight had started. The engine owns
the dark (settled at charting, from §9: "it never decides that the torch went out"), so the
block that mentions the lantern is the block that has to say so.

**The ALERT band vocabulary is deliberately not decided here.** It is emberdelve-ffi.2's —
what is on the LIGHT and ALERT tables, and the signs under them. This ticket leaves it a
named slot rather than pre-empting the ticket that owns it.

## The objective

A **state line plus a closed-world sentence**.

The objective is an engine-owned prop (emberdelve-4h9.4), so it is already listed under
`## What the player can see` or `## Hidden`. What that listing cannot express is that the
party is *carrying it out of a room the prop no longer belongs to* — which is the whole
reason §15 calls this the expensive part of M4. Hence `objective: not yet found` /
`objective: carried by <name>`.

"There is nothing else here worth carrying out. Do not invent a second." is the `## Ways out`
lesson applied *before* the playtest instead of after it. A block vague about state is worse
than no block, because the model fills the gap and is then consistent about the wrong thing.

## Consumables

**All three counters, always, zeroes included.** `potions: 0 · torches: 1 · rope: 0`.

An omitted line is an invitation — the argument this codebase already makes three times over
(an empty tool enum, an empty `## Ways out`, an empty `## Secrets`). §9 is blunt that the
model always says yes, so the block's job is to stop the narrator handing over a potion
nobody has. Enforcement stays `use_item`'s rejection; the block is honesty, not a gate.

These are counts and they stay counts under the rule above: `use_item` takes a consumable
and the model has to know whether it can call it.

## Always present, never conditional

The block is always there, following `## Ways out`'s precedent rather than `## Momentum`'s or
`## Secrets`'.

A conditional pressure block makes its **absence** information, and the model will read that
absence as "no pressure" on exactly the turn a clock starts running. Always-present also
means the block's shape never changes mid-session, which is the property that stopped
`## Ways out` being re-improvised every turn.

## Where the rules live

**Facts in the projection, permissions in the prompts, nothing said twice.** The
`worldState(boolean forProse)` split already works this way — the two models are told the
same facts and given opposite permissions. One exception: "never read a hit point aloud" is a
standing rule rather than a per-turn fact, so it stays in `dm.md`, where it already is.

No new text in `dm.md` or `dm-tools.md` for any of the above. AGENTS.md's finding stands —
writing more about brevity made the model more verbose, and terse instructions win. The
fact-not-cue line inside the block is the only instruction added anywhere, and it is two
sentences.

## Term collision, resolved

`CONTEXT.md:123` defined **Clock** as the ordered narration queue (`godot/autoload/clock.gd`);
§9's `Clock` record is a ticking counter with three scales. §9's keeps the name — it is the one
with a campaign-scale future and a design document naming it. The glossary entry for the Godot
one is renamed to **Narration queue**, noting `clock.gd` as its file, and a **Delve clock**
entry added. Glossary-only: renaming `clock.gd` is a build-side chore that can follow or never,
and `Clock.hold` reads correctly in AGENTS.md as it stands.

## Not decided here

**How the narrator conveys a downed party member.** `emberdelve-4h9.13` and the map's fog list
both hoped this would fold into this ticket. It does not: the band vocabulary above bottoms out
at "barely standing", which is a creature still on its feet, and downed is a different state
with a clock attached. Graduated to its own ticket.

title: M4 wayfinder — settle the delve design before it is built
description:
## Destination

A signed M4 design spec at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-XX-m4-delve-design.md` — the document
emberdelve-4h9's ten build children get executed against. §9 of `docs/ai-dm-system-design.md` is
explicit that it is "a bet, not a record", written at lower confidence than everything above it;
this map settles what it left open so that no build session has to stop and decide.

The map ends when the spec is signed. The gate session itself (play it, write `m4-evaluation.md`)
is a child of 4h9, not of this map.

## Notes

Domain: the Emberdelve delve loop. Read `AGENTS.md` first (it wins over the design doc where the
two disagree), then `docs/ai-dm-system-design.md` §9, then `CONTEXT.md`.

Every session on this map calls the `grilling` and `domain-modeling` skills unless the ticket's
own type says otherwise. Prototype tickets call `prototype`.

**Plan, don't do.** Tickets here resolve decisions. The building happens under emberdelve-4h9.

**Amend 4h9 in place.** When a decision here lands, `bd update` whichever 4h9 child it supersedes,
so the build ticket is always true. A build ticket that contradicts the spec is the copper-key
failure applied to process: durable, consistent, and pointing at a lock that is not there.

**The `Ending` enum is descriptive, never a verdict.** `EXTRACTED_WITH_OBJECTIVE` /
`EXTRACTED_WITHOUT` / `PARTY_LOST`, not WON/LOST. §9's own first argument for bounded sites is that
"a cleared site is a durable fact" the campaign layer consumes. Scoring the delve here pre-empts
§10, and the standing design intent is that a bad outcome must never guarantee campaign failure —
player creativity and DM improvisation should be able to open another path. An enum that judges
takes that away.

## Settled at charting — 2026-09-08

The grilling session that produced this map settled twenty-four decisions. They are the spec's raw
material and are recorded here because they are not tickets and have nowhere else to live.

**The delve ends as an event.** `DelveEnded`, folded into `WorldState` and shipped in `SceneState`,
under invariant 8 — the end of a delve is the most important thing that happens in a session and
must be in the log and must replay. Three endings; only `PARTY_LOST` is losing. Extracting
empty-handed is a legitimate cautious outcome, because §9's greed decision only works if leaving
early is respectable. `godot/chrome/defeat.gd`'s client-side `hp <= 0` check on a hardcoded
`"fighter"` goes: it cannot distinguish three endings and it names a singleton player against
invariant 2.

**Light moves from the room to the party.** `room.gd:315` builds wall torches from the room's own
`LightingPreset`; `Room.Level` is a separate axis and the file is emphatic about not confusing
them. So a LIGHT clock has nothing to burn down — the party carries no light. It does now: a
carried lantern, fuelled by the LIGHT clock, read as a shrinking radius. Room torches stay
room-owned so `Level.DIM` keeps its one meaning. The 2026-09-07 playtest recorded that invented
lanterns already travel with the party as facts with no prop behind them, and `kaykit_halloween`
ships an unused `lantern_standing`: this is the hotdog problem solved the cheap way round, by
giving the board the thing the fiction keeps inventing.

**The engine owns the dark.** No DM lighting tool, in either phase. §9: "The DM narrates what the
table produced; it never decides that the torch went out." A narrator that can turn the lights off
will do it because it is dramatic rather than because anything was spent, and then the clock means
nothing. Scarcity is the engine's alone.

**A failed check ticks the light clock one segment; a natural 1 ticks two.** §9 already names noisy
failures as a tick trigger. Any-failure-alone taxes trying things; nat-1-alone is too rare to build
pressure across 4-5 rooms. The natural die is already special (invariant 5). This is also the
reconciliation of a real play observation: the DM narrating a dropped lantern on a 1 was the right
beat reached the wrong way — now the engine ticks, the table fires, and the DM narrates a real
event.

**The `torch` consumable refuels the light clock.** §9's Consumable enum is already potion / torch
/ rope. This links the counter map to the clock and states the greed loop in one line: how deep you
go is how many torches you brought. It also keeps the clock non-terminal.

**Clocks cannot kill.** The clock's job is to make leaving attractive, not to be a second health
bar. A terminal clock turns the delve into a speedrun; §9 wants a greed decision. Death follows
from a filled light clock indirectly, which is enough.

**Clocks speak twice.** A threshold fires a sign; the fill fires the consequence. Signs are §9's
region-scale "spoor, smoke, tracks" brought to delve scale — engine-fired, table-driven, narrated
by the DM. A clock that speaks only at full is a jump scare; one that speaks every tick is a
counter with extra steps.

**The clock is diegetic and unlabelled.** No segment counter on screen. The LIGHT clock reads as
the shrinking radius; the ALERT clock's entire read is its signs. One legible clock beats two
half-legible ones, and the projection lets the DM foreshadow the alert clock honestly.

**Rest exists, and it is the pressure valve.** An explicit player action; only in a room with no
living hostile in it; ticks every running clock one segment; restores a fixed small amount. Not a
roll — the dice are for questions the DM is about to answer, and "how much did you recover" is not
a moment. Fixed and small keeps the arithmetic in the player's head, which is where the tension is.

**Downed is a clock.** 0 HP drops you and starts a short clock; if it fills before combat ends, the
delve is lost. Not death saves — that is §6 and it belongs to the next milestone. The plain
instant-death alternative makes "5 hit points in front of a door" already-lost rather than tense,
at HP 12 against 1d6+2. A downed clock uses the primitive being built anyway, at a scale it is
already sized for, and stays correct when the party grows past one.

**`EnvTorchlit`'s 1.1 ambient is a prerequisite, rescoped to one number.** emberdelve-27l. A
shrinking light radius cannot be judged at ambient 1.1. Scoped to changing the number and looking
once, so the lighting anti-goal's timebox holds.

**Structure.** This map is a sibling of 4h9, not its parent and not its child: "what can I decide"
and "what can I build" are different sessions and `bd ready` should tell them apart. The spec is
written in one pass at the end, from the resolution comments — M1/M2/M3's specs read as documents
with an argument, and a case written in eight sittings by eight agents is not one.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket -->

- [What the projection carries about hurt, clocks and the objective](emberdelve-ffi.1): one
  always-present `## The party` block above `## Entities present`, carrying hurt, the clocks, the
  objective's state and all three consumable counts. **A count that drives a tool decision stays a
  count; a count that only describes state becomes a band** — which is why `## Momentum` keeps its
  number and hurt loses its fraction. Hurt uses `BeatRenderer.condition()`'s existing four bands,
  extracted so there is one wound vocabulary. `DmService.java:797`'s `5/12 hp`, which no decision
  ever asked for, goes. Facts in the projection, permissions in the prompts, nothing said twice.

- [What is on the LIGHT and ALERT tables, and the signs under them](emberdelve-ffi.2): four tables,
  written out. **A consequence may only do what a tool can already do** — a named, pre-validated
  bundle of events that already have an `Event` + `Diff` pair, never an effect language. **A sign is
  a consequence whose bundle is empty**, so there is one enum and one firing path. LIGHT is a fixed
  one-entry table (`LIGHT_OUT`), because a clock you can plan against is what makes the greed
  decision computable; ALERT is drawn from four, because its entire read is its signs. Signs ride
  the latched directive rail and cost no model call. Rooms and rests tick both clocks; failed checks
  tick LIGHT; fights and a filled LIGHT tick ALERT — declared on the tick side, never inside a
  consequence. ALERT resets on fill, LIGHT stays full until a torch. `Disposition { HOSTILE, WARY }`
  — a consequence brings something in, it does not decide how the meeting goes. Also takes
  [emberdelve-vy7](emberdelve-vy7)'s answer: `start_combat` stays for provoked fights, the
  two-failure escalation rule goes, and the ALERT clock becomes the only source of an unprovoked one.

- [The numbers — tune attrition until 5 hit points is a real decision](emberdelve-ffi.6): fighter
  **HP 12 → 20**, goblin weakened to **AC 12 / HP 6 / +3 / 1d4+1**, new brute **AC 13 / HP 16 / +4 /
  1d8+2**. Rest restores 4, a potion 8; LIGHT and ALERT are 6 segments; 2 torches, 2 potions; a site
  is 5 rooms with ~3 fights. **The ticket's premise was wrong** — at HP 12, five hit points against a
  goblin is a 72% survival, median loss per fight *zero*. The finding that unlocked it: **the
  encounter decides where the doubt window sits, max hit points decide how much bar is above it**,
  and conflating those two is what made attrition untunable. The brute lands the window on **4–10,
  45.7% survival at exactly 5**, making §9's gate sentence arithmetically true. Against a party of
  one the action economy inverts the obvious ladder — N weak enemies is always harder than one strong
  one — which is why the goblin had to become the mob it was already described as. **Two charting
  reversals:** an ordinary failed check no longer ticks LIGHT (only a natural 1 does, one segment),
  because measured sessions differ sevenfold in failure rate on the DM's choice of DC and that hands
  scarcity to the narrator; and the downed clock is dropped, because `isOver()` ends the fight when
  the only player-controlled entity drops, so it can never fill. Numbers reproducible from
  `docs/evidence/m4-attrition-sim.py`.

- [EnvTorchlit's 1.1 ambient is the suspect number, not EnvDim's 0.7](emberdelve-27l): **1.1 → 0.7**,
  judged by looking at the crypt at all four camera corners rather than by reading numbers
  (`godot/dev/light_shots.gd` renders it through the real client — no server, no key, no session).
  **The playtest comparison it rested on had two variables in it:** the crypt seen from the gallery
  also has its wall fires out, because `room.gd` only burns the torches of the room the party is in.
  Crossing both axes showed the ambient does not light the floor at all — the torch pools own it at
  every value down to 0.35 — and that what 1.1 bought was a **blue-violet wash on the wall margins**,
  which is exactly the surface a shrinking radius has to leave. It does not collapse TORCHLIT into
  DIM: at equal energy TORCHLIT still sits 1.67× above it on colour alone. **Carried forward:** 0.7
  still shows the whole room's layout, so it is right for a torchlit room and probably too high for a
  room the lantern is the only light in — `EnvDark`'s 0.35 territory, which is
  [How the shrinking light radius reads](emberdelve-ffi.5)'s problem. **What the sheets turned up
  that the ticket did not ask:** the crypt looks better with the wall fires out, and that is not a
  taste call — both recorded sessions describe a chamber lit by two green braziers and nothing else,
  eleven times in the M3 session alone. The board has been contradicting the DM. Split into
  [The crypt is lit by its braziers, not by wall torches](emberdelve-4h9.16) for the build, and
  [Which clock moves a room's fires, and in which direction](emberdelve-ffi.9) for the decision.

- [Which clock moves a room's fires, and in which direction](emberdelve-ffi.9): **ALERT owns the
  dial, and the room says which way it turns.** Every fill moves the party's current room one step
  in the direction that room authored; a room has exactly two light states, ever, and it ratchets —
  a torch relights nothing, because a torch is the party's and the fires are the room's. **The
  ticket's two proposals were both already answered**: [What is on the LIGHT and ALERT
  tables](emberdelve-ffi.2) had put THE_DARK_CLOSES_IN on the ALERT table, so LIGHT-empties-the-room
  said the same thing on a second clock and ALERT-lights-the-torches pointed the same clock the
  other way, jittering the dial with the draw. **The frequency was a number, not a preference:** ~15
  ALERT ticks a delve against 6 segments is 2–3 fills, so a 1-in-4 draw is 0.6 fire-moves and most
  runs would never see the site change. Unconditional on fill it is 2–3 rooms of five, every delve —
  declared on the tick side by the same precedent that kept "LIGHT filling ticks ALERT" out of
  LIGHT_OUT. THE_DARK_CLOSES_IN retires as a `ConsequenceId`; its no-spawn slot survives as
  **IT_PASSES_BY**, an entry with an empty bundle, which ffi.2's own "a sign is a consequence whose
  bundle is empty" already makes legal. **Two live defects in a closed ticket, fixed here:** the
  projection never states a room's lighting and `crypt.json`'s overview hardcodes "lit green by two
  braziers", so THE_DARK_CLOSES_IN as signed off would darken the board under prose that cannot
  follow — the copper key with its polarity reversed; and a draw landing on a room already at `DARK`
  logged a `ConsequenceFired` that did nothing, now fixed by filtering at draw. **A room's lighting
  stops being authored content and becomes folded state** — `RoomDefinition.lighting` is the initial
  value, `GameEngine.roomView()` reads the fold. Content shape: a `fires { lit, to, moved }` object,
  where `lit` and `moved` are the one fire line that is true at a time and `to` names the moved
  preset outright so nothing reads an ordering into a closed enum. `Room.Level` is untouched and the
  separate-axis rule becomes load-bearing rather than merely true. **The site must exercise both
  directions or lose one:** at least one authored room moves brighter, or `BRIGHTER` comes out —
  an unexercised direction is AGENTS.md's measured "a capability flag is a claim, not a behaviour".

- [What the carried lantern is, as an object](emberdelve-ffi.3): **it is a torch, and as an object it
  is nothing new.** §9 already calls it one (`docs/ai-dm-system-design.md:612` — "it never decides
  that the torch went out"), a torch is not lantern fuel, and `kaykit_dungeon` ships the handheld
  pair `torch.gltf` / `torch_lit.gltf`; the `lantern_standing` charting cited is floor dressing. The
  party's light is a **pure function of the LIGHT clock** — no `Lantern` record, no new fold entry,
  not a `Prop` (`Diff` has no `PropMoved`). What ships is a closed **`PartyLight { FULL, LOW,
  GUTTERING, FAILING, OUT }`**, whose five names are `ffi.2`'s own sign names, so **what the DM
  narrates and what the player sees are the same five words**. Not the segment count — the wire
  should be unable to carry the counter that must never be drawn — and not a radius, because
  appearance numbers live on the client. **Split the nodes:** the pool is one `OmniLight3D` owned by
  `World` following the party (a `Room` would spend `MAX_TORCH_LIGHTS`, a token is freed on every
  crossing, a hand bone swings with the chop); the mesh rides `handslot.l`, which `Knight.glb` has
  free and animated. **Never a pick target** — `brazier-east` at hand height, moving every turn — so
  spending a torch becomes a **button**, and the potion and the rest join it on an exploration
  action bar. That amends 4h9.2's "no UI beyond a count" on the door's principle, *a button per
  player action the DM does not adjudicate*, since none of the three is a question the DM answers.
  **Exploration-only is a finding, not a scope call:** `m4-attrition-sim.py:60`'s `fight()` heals
  nobody, so ffi.6's 45.7%-at-5 was measured with no in-combat healing in it. **Surfaced a defect in
  signed-off ground:** `DmService.pendingArrival` is a single `String` about to have five writers,
  last write wins silently, and an overwritten sign is a clock that went quiet — filed on
  [The Clock primitive](emberdelve-4h9.3) as an ordered list. Whether a crossing narrates at all
  reopens as [Whether crossing a threshold narrates](emberdelve-ffi.10), because the argument that
  reopens it — signs now fire on room entry — did not exist when play judged the silence right.

## Not yet specified

- **The ambient sound bed the signs would eventually want.** `AGENTS.md` records that there is none
  at all — "the braziers burn without a sound". An alert clock is a reason to build one, but
  building it *for* the clock is the tail wagging the dog. Revisit once signs exist and have
  something to be about.
- **Whether "something worth more, deeper" needs a value concept.** §9's greed decision wants
  something past the objective worth going for. Whether that is a second objective-shaped prop or
  something with a value on it is not decidable until the site is being authored.
- **Whether generated rooms need a safe-room concept.** Resting is room-conditional (no living
  hostile). That rule is engine-owned and survives generation, but whether the generator has to
  guarantee a restable room is a question for the generator milestone.

## Out of scope

Ruled beyond this destination. These do not graduate.

- **Meta-progression** — stash, upgrades, run tiers. §9: never. It competes with the campaign layer
  for the same design space.
- **Whether a room's light state carries between delves** — was fog until
  [Which clock moves a room's fires](emberdelve-ffi.9) answered its precondition. A site left dark
  is a durable fact of the same kind §9 says a cleared site is, and durable facts between runs are
  the campaign layer's. M4 has no campaign layer and does not resume from a log, so within this
  destination the answer is no; it returns only if the destination is redrawn.
- **Resume from a session log, snapshotting, schema migration** — §16. Sting comes from within the
  session; a lost delve costs the run, and the run is the session.
- **Inventory, equipment, encumbrance** — §16. Consumables are a counter map and nothing more.
- **The effect interpreter and the stance layer** — §15 puts them with the content milestone,
  together, because each is a tax alone.
- **The region and the watch loop** — §16.
- **`WATCH` and `FRONT` clock scales** — the enum carries all three because the record is built
  once; only DELVE is in scope.
- **A DM lighting tool** — see Settled above.
- **Terminal clocks** — see Settled above.
- **The downed clock, and how a downed member reads to the narrator** — settled at charting, ruled
  out by [The numbers](emberdelve-ffi.6). `CombatEngine.isOver()` ends the fight when no living
  player-controlled entity remains, so at party size one the clock is inert by construction, and the
  "five hit points is one bad roll from over" premise it rested on measured false. 0 hp is
  `PARTY_LOST`. Closed: [emberdelve-4h9.13](emberdelve-4h9.13) and
  [How a downed party member reads to the narrator](emberdelve-ffi.8), the latter existing only to
  decide questions the downed state raised. Re-enters with a second party member or §6's death saves.
- **§10 judging a delve's outcome** — the `Ending` enum stays descriptive so that it can, later.
- **The M4 gate session and `m4-evaluation.md`** — filed as a child of emberdelve-4h9. The gate is
  what the spec is for, not a step on the way to it.
acceptance_criteria: A signed spec at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-XX-m4-delve-design.md, every child ticket closed with a resolution comment, and nothing left to decide before emberdelve-4h9's children can be built. AGENTS.md and CONTEXT.md updated to match.

title: M4 — Can you lose a delve, and does losing it sting?
description:
M4. Gate question, from docs/ai-dm-system-design.md section 9: can you lose a delve,
and does losing it sting?

Stated as something to feel, not to measure, in the same spirit as M0. You should be
able to stand in front of a door at 5 hit points and genuinely not know whether to
open it. If you can, the loop exists.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE GENERATOR

M1's outstanding half (LayoutGenerator, ExitPlacer, world-space packing) is the other
candidate and it loses on three counts.

1. The design doc already ruled on the ordering. Section 15, Still ahead: "Prove it on
   authored rooms before generated ones, or a generator bug and a game-feel problem are
   indistinguishable."
2. M3's own carry-forward is the evidence. "Generated rooms still have nothing to find.
   PropPlacer marks nothing hidden, so reveal_prop is never offered." That is not a
   missing feature in PropPlacer, it is PropPlacer written without knowing what a room
   is for. LayoutGenerator would be written against the same unknown, and a dungeon that
   generates six rooms with nothing to find is the M1 hole multiplied by six.
3. Risk 2 in section 17 is the top live risk and generation makes it worse. "Nothing is
   scarce, so nothing is at stake... the game runs on novelty, which decays in about
   twenty minutes." More rooms is more novelty. It buys nothing against that risk.

M3 already paid most of the setup. Section 9 lists "party state is session-scoped, not
room-scoped" as the small refactor everything else depends on. GameEngine.java:73 spawns
the party once at the entrance and entities live in WorldState.entities across
crossExit, so that refactor looks done, pending the audit in the first child.

WHAT IS IN

Attrition (session-scoped party state, scarce healing, consumables as a counter map),
the Clock primitive at DELVE scale, an engine-owned objective that is takeable, an exit
that checks for it, a delve that can be lost, clickable props, DM-placed markers, a
4-5 room authored site, and more than one enemy on the board at once.

WHAT IS OUT, AND STAYS OUT

The effect interpreter and the stance layer. Section 15 puts them with the content
milestone, together, because each is a tax alone. Several skeletons in one room is N
instances of one or two stat blocks against the existing ~40-line resolveAttack. It is
not permission to open section 6.

Inventory, equipment, encumbrance. Section 16 has the re-entry condition. Consumables
are a counter map and nothing more.

The region and the watch loop. Section 16 defers them until enough sites exist that
travelling between them means something.

Meta-progression. Section 9: never. It competes with the campaign layer for the same
design space.

THE ANTI-GOAL THIS RETIRES

AGENTS.md, Anti-goals: "Do not add a third room." That was M3-scoped and it is spent.
A delve needs enough rooms for "push deeper or get out" to be a real decision. The
generator anti-goal stands until this epic closes.

ORDER

Prove it on authored rooms. The generator comes after, with a spec: the authored site
is what LayoutGenerator has to be able to produce.
acceptance_criteria:
A played session, in the real Godot client, in which the player takes the objective and
chooses between leaving with it and going deeper, and a second played session in which
the delve is lost. Both written to server/sessions/ and one copied into docs/evidence/
so it replays in the suite. Judged the way M0 and M3 were judged: an evaluation doc with
a verdict, not a metric.
notes:
THE DESIGN IS ON A WAYFINDER MAP 2026-09-08: emberdelve-ffi, "M4 wayfinder — settle the delve design
before it is built". Read its `## Settled at charting` block before opening any child of this epic.

The two trees answer different questions. **This epic is what gets built; the map is what gets

Five children were missing and have been filed: 4h9.11 (rest), 4h9.12 (the party carries a light),
4h9.13 (downed is a clock), 4h9.14 (the projection carries the delve — §15's "expensive part", which

The map's destination is a signed spec at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-XX-m4-delve-design.md`.

title: Doors read as shut but every exit is always passable
description:
Playtest 2026-09-07, two sessions. The player could not tell whether a door was locked, unlocked, or crossable yet, and the DM answered differently every turn.

crossExit (GameEngine.java:284) gates on combat and nothing else. There is no shut, locked or barred state anywhere. Every exit is passable at all times outside a fight.

Every authored door description asserts the opposite:
- crypt door-north: 'banded in tarnished iron. It has no handle on this side.'
- gallery door-south: 'The slab door back to the crypt, shut on a dark stair-head.'

Nothing resolves the conflict for the model. waysOut() emits only '- a way out in the north wall' with no state. The use_exit schema says 'Only when the player has said they are leaving' and dm-tools.md:39 closes with 'When in doubt, do not.' So the model holds a sealed-sounding description, a bare ways-out line, and a refusal bias, and re-improvises the reconciliation every turn.

Both sessions independently invented an ATHLETICS DC 20 kick to open the door. The check adjudicated nothing: the door was open before the roll and open after. Session 2 also spent two turns trying a found copper key on a lock that does not exist.

This is fix (a): make the prompt tell the truth. Fix (b), modelling a real shut/locked exit, is filed separately.
acceptance_criteria: waysOut() states that a listed way out can be taken at any time outside a fight. Gallery door-south no longer asserts the door is shut. Crypt door-north keeps 'no handle on this side' — true of a door that still shoves open. Server suite green.
close_reason: waysOut() now states every listed exit is open, unlocked and crossable outside a fight; gallery door-south no longer says shut. Two tests lock it. Server suite green.
