title: Whether crossing a threshold narrates, now that signs ride the rail
description:
## Question

Does clicking a door run a prose phase?

Today it does not. `WsHandler.enterExit` sends the new Scene, calls `dm.noteCrossing`, and stops;
`DmService.takePendingArrival` (`DmService.java:952`) is only ever consumed by a free-text prose
phase, which the click path never runs. So a crossing is silent and its arrival directive waits for
whatever the player types next.

**Play judged that right, and the judgement stands on its own terms.** 2026-09-07: 15 of 17
crossings across two sessions produced no narration, and neither player remarked on it. AGENTS.md
records the reason — clicking a door and walking through *is* the honest path, and the arrival beat
was not what was missing. `emberdelve-xgg.12` is that finding, recorded and deliberately not
scheduled.

## What changed

**The rail now carries clock traffic.** `emberdelve-4h9.12` settled that every room entry ticks
LIGHT, including a room already visited — so a LIGHT sign can fire *on a crossing*. With crossings
silent, that sign sits on the rail until the next typed turn, and the clock speaks late, attached to
whatever the player did next.

That failure already has a recorded instance. `emberdelve-xgg.12` logged a stale "you have come back"
directive landing 16 seconds later on a key-searching turn, after two rapid crossings. Under M4 the
same mechanism drops a sign instead of misplacing a pleasantry, and a clock that goes quiet is the
thing `emberdelve-ffi.2` built a sign table to prevent.

## What has to be decided

- **Does every crossing narrate, or only one that has something on the rail?** The second is cheaper
  and reads as the DM speaking when there is something to say. It is also a rule the player will
  reverse-engineer: silence starts meaning nothing happened.
- **Where the ordered rail from `emberdelve-4h9.3` is drained.** One prose call per crossing, or one
  per directive.
- **Whether an arrival line and a sign in the same crossing are one beat or two.**
- **What happens on rapid crossings.** `emberdelve-xgg.12` observed gallery→crypt→gallery in three
  seconds, which pushed two threshold markers into `history` with no reply between them.
- **`tryLock` or `lock`.** AGENTS.md § *Combat narration*: narration the player asked for waits on
  the lock; narration the engine generated gives up. A crossing is player-asked, but a sign is
  engine-generated, and they arrive together.

## The cost, measured

`emberdelve-ffi.9` puts a delve at ~9 room entries — the entrance is also the exit. `openScene` runs
515–712ms to first token and 1.8–3.1s total, and a crossing already has cover: the camera moves and a
room draws. AGENTS.md — "Speech latency is only expensive when nothing covers it."

## Prior art

`emberdelve-xgg.12` carries the sketch: a `narrateArrival(TurnSink)` modelled on
`DmService.openScene` (`DmService.java:177`), `takePendingArrival()` as the directive, `tryLock`
rather than `lock`, and one submit in `enterExit`. `turnSink(ctx)` already exists. That ticket is the
build; this one is the decision.
acceptance_criteria: A decision on whether a crossing runs a prose phase, on whether it is conditional on the rail having something in it, and on how an arrival line and a clock sign arriving together are ordered. Enough for emberdelve-xgg.12 to be built.

title: Which clock moves a room's fires, and in which direction
description:
## Question

A room's fires are currently a fact about the room, decided once when it is built and never touched
again. Should a clock move them in play, and if so which clock and in which direction?

Two proposals, and they point opposite ways on the same dial:

- **LIGHT fills -> the room's braziers go out.** The site goes dark around the party. Room-scale
  and unmissable, where a radius contracting around the party is a quiet signal -- which is the
  complaint that made emberdelve-ffi.5 a ticket in the first place. It lands the fiction the
  sessions already wrote: fires that "should have burned out centuries ago" finally doing it.

- **ALERT fills -> the wall torches get lit.** The site is awake and looking for you. This gives
  the wall torches a reason to exist at all after emberdelve-4h9.16 takes them out of the crypt,
  and it makes the two clocks read as one visible dial moved from both ends.

WHAT MAKES THIS A DECISION AND NOT A FEATURE

**It changes what the LIGHT and ALERT consequence tables settled** (emberdelve-4h9.3, resolved on
this map). Those tables were written when the only thing light meant was the party's lantern. If
room fires move too, some entries on them are now saying the same thing twice.

**Two different fictions.** Braziers going out says *the crypt is going dark*. The LIGHT clock's
fiction is *your lamp is failing* -- and that is the one the party can spend a torch to fix. If a
torch resets LIGHT to empty (emberdelve-ffi.6), does it relight the braziers? If not, the dial only
travels one way and the clock is not really driving it.

**Under invariant 8 a fire going out is a state change, so it is an event and a diff, not a client
flourish.** Confirmed as the wanted shape 2026-09-10. That means a room's fire state has to be
foldable from the log and shipped in RoomView, which is a change to what a room *is* -- today
`lighting` is authored content that never varies. It also has to replay: --replay must produce the
same dark crypt.

**It is site content, not a general rule.** It only works in rooms that have braziers, and only
where wall brackets exist to light. That is a constraint on emberdelve-4h9.8's authored site, so
this has to be decided before the site is authored.

WHY IT IS WORTH THE WEIGHT

The reason offered for it, and the one to test the answer against: changing light state room by
room is what makes a second playthrough different from the first. A site that is dark where it was
lit, or lit where it was dark, is a different site without new content -- which is the cheapest
kind of variety this project can buy, and M4 has exactly one authored site.

Depends on emberdelve-ffi.5 only insofar as both are about how light reads; they can be taken in
either order, but the radius question is the narrower one.
close_reason: ALERT owns the dial; every fill moves the party's current room one step in the direction that room authored. One-way, two states per room, a fires{lit,to,moved} object in the room file. THE_DARK_CLOSES_IN retired as a ConsequenceId, replaced on the table by IT_PASSES_BY (empty bundle). Room lighting becomes folded state, not authored content. Resolution comment has the arithmetic and the two ffi.2 defects it fixes.

comments.author: hampton.black
comments.text:
# Resolution — 2026-09-10

The dial exists, it lives on **ALERT**, and **the room says which way it turns**.

Every ALERT fill moves the party's current room one step, in the direction that room authored.
A room has exactly two light states, ever: as authored, and moved. It ratchets — a moved room
stays moved for the delve, a second fill there changes no light, and a spent torch relights
nothing. A torch is the party's; the fires are the room's.

## The ticket's two proposals were both already answered

There was an answer on the board before this ticket was written. `emberdelve-ffi.2` put
**THE_DARK_CLOSES_IN** — "Room lighting drops one level" — on the ALERT table as a drawn
consequence, explicitly sanctioned as "legitimate here, as an engine-fired consequence, where it
was ruled out as a DM tool."

So this was never "should a clock move the fires":

- **Proposal A** (LIGHT fills -> braziers out) said the same thing on a second clock, and would
  have spent the one thing the map deliberately bought — `ffi.2` made LIGHT a *fixed one-entry*
  table because "a clock you can plan against is what makes the greed decision computable".
- **Proposal B** (ALERT -> wall torches lit) pointed the *same* clock the other way, so the draw
  would have jittered the dial back and forth between fills.

Its stated motivations were also weaker than they read. "Gives the wall torches a reason to exist
after `emberdelve-4h9.16` takes them out of the crypt" — they already have one: the gallery is
`DIM`, which is `TORCH_SPACING` 5, so it has them.

The replayability case, though, is **stronger** than the ticket claimed, for a reason it did not
name: `emberdelve-4h9.8`'s entrance is also the exit, so the party walks the site twice. A room
that goes dark behind you is a room you re-cross on the way out. The dial pays off inside one
delve, not only across playthroughs.

## The number that decided the frequency

`ffi.6` pins both clocks at 6 segments and the site at 5 rooms with ~3 fights; `ffi.2`'s tick
table gives ALERT +1 per room entered, +1 per rest, +1 per fight start, +1 when LIGHT fills. With
the exit being the entrance that is ~9 room entries, not 5:

    ~9 rooms + 3 fights + ~2 LIGHT fills + ~1 rest  =  ~15 ticks
    ALERT resets on fill, 6 segments                =  ~2-3 fills per delve

At `ffi.2`'s 1-in-4 draw that is **0.6 fire-moves per delve** — most runs would never see the site
change at all, which is not enough to carry the argument the ticket rests on. Unconditional on
fill it is **2-3 rooms of a five-room site, every delve**.

That is why the fire-move is not a table entry. It is declared on the **fill** side, by the
precedent `ffi.2` set when it put "LIGHT filling ticks ALERT" on the tick side rather than burying
it inside LIGHT_OUT: a clock that ticks a clock through a consequence is the first step toward a
state machine nobody can trace.

## The ALERT table after this

**THE_DARK_CLOSES_IN is retired as a `ConsequenceId`** — its effect is now unconditional and
needs no name. Its *slot* survives, because `ffi.2`'s reason for it survives: "a table that always
spawns something is a table the player reads as 'a fight is coming' after two draws."

Replaced by **IT_PASSES_BY** — something came near and went on. An entry with an **empty bundle**,
which costs nothing structurally because `ffi.2`'s own unification already makes it legal: *a sign
is a consequence whose bundle is empty*. Same record, same table, same firing path.

| ConsequenceId | Bundle | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| PATROL_ARRIVES | EntitySpawned in the party's room + ... | HOSTILE |
| SOMETHING_WANDERS_IN | EntitySpawned in the party's room | WARY |
| IT_PASSES_BY | *(empty)* | — |
| DRAWN_BY_THE_NOISE | EntityMoved — a hostile already in the site | HOSTILE |

The lights changing therefore becomes the loudest diegetic sign in the game, and the clock still
carries no label — `ffi.2`'s "diegetic and unlabelled" holds. A quarter of the time nothing
follows, so it reads as a **threat rather than a promise**, which is the read the drawn table was
protecting in the first place.

## Two defects in a closed ticket, live today with no new dial at all

**1. The narrator is never told what a room's lighting is.**
`DmService.worldState()` prints `## Room: <name>`, then the authored `overview` and `sensory`, and
never states the lighting. `crypt.json`'s overview is *"Cold, close, and lit green by two braziers
that should have burned out centuries ago"*; `sensory` adds *"The braziers hiss."* Fire
THE_DARK_CLOSES_IN exactly as `ffi.2` signed it off and the board goes dark while the DM goes on
describing green braziers — **the copper key with its polarity reversed**: the board changing
under prose that cannot follow it.

**2. A draw can land on a consequence the room cannot honour.**
THE_DARK_CLOSES_IN in a room already at `DARK` fires, logs a `ConsequenceFired`, and changes
nothing. `4h9.16` is about to push the crypt toward the bottom of that scale. **Fixed by filtering
at draw**: the table draws only from entries that would change something. `ffi.2` logs the drawn
id specifically so a session where something appeared from nowhere can be diagnosed — "the file
that proves it is already on disk" — and a logged consequence that did nothing is a log that lies
about what happened, which is the same objection that got bundled-events-only refused. Filtering
subsumes a per-room table declaration, and replay is unaffected because the drawn id is carried,
never recomputed.

## The content shape

A room carries a `fires` object; a room without one has no fires and never moves.

    "fires": {
      "lit":   "Lit green by two braziers that should have burned out centuries ago.",
      "to":    "DARK",
      "moved": "The braziers have gone out — the green light is gone and the cold in here is
                the cold of the stone."
    }

`to` names the moved `LightingPreset` outright rather than a direction, so nothing reads an
ordering into a closed enum (invariant 7) and a room cannot step twice. `to`/`moved` are an
optional pair: fires that never move are allowed.

**Derived, not asked, and it extends the answer to Q5.** Requiring the overview to stop stating
the fire state means the *unmoved* fire line needs somewhere to live too, or the DM has no fire
description at all on an ordinary delve. Hence `lit` alongside `moved`: exactly one fire line is
true at any moment, and it is printed in the room block after `sensory`.

The precedent for the *wrong* fix is already in `crypt.json`. `dmNotes.theDoor` ends: "Anything
the player was told earlier about it being sealed was true of a door that had not been unlocked
yet; do not restate it as though it still cannot open." That paragraph exists because the door's
state changed and the authored prose could not. It works, and it is a workaround for a schema that
cannot vary. This one is changing the schema, so it does not need the workaround.

## What this makes a room

**A room's lighting stops being authored content and becomes folded state.**
`RoomDefinition.lighting` becomes the *initial* value; `GameEngine.roomView()` reads the fold
instead of `structure.lighting()`, defaulting to the authored one. This is the change to what a
room *is* that the ticket predicted, and it is the only one.

`Room.Level` is untouched and stays a separate axis — `room.gd:91` is emphatic about that, and
this decision makes the distinction load-bearing rather than merely true: the room's lighting now
varies, the render level still does not.

## The machinery, all of it forced

- `Event.RoomLightingChanged(at, roomId, from, to)`. Invariant 8: a fire going out is a state
  change, so it is an event and the fold is the only reader. It rides the schema bump `ffi.2`
  already filed against `emberdelve-4h9.3` for `ClockTicked` and `ConsequenceFired`, so it costs
  no second refused-log.
- `Diff.RoomLightingChanged(roomId, lighting)`. `ffi.2` already filed "Room lighting has no Diff"
  as build work; this is what it is for.
- `WorldState.lightingIn(roomId)`, folded, defaulting to the authored preset.
- **The projection**: the room block prints `fires.lit` or `fires.moved` after `sensory`. Standing
  state, every turn, for as long as it is true.
- **The beat**: the move latches a **one-clause directive** on the same rail as a sign
  (`pendingArrival`'s, not `narrateCombat`'s), in ARRIVAL_FIRST's register. The directive says it
  just happened; the projection line keeps it true afterwards. `ffi.2`'s measured warning applies
  unchanged — one clause, never a paragraph about what the dark means.

## What the client has to do

`world.gd:126` rebuilds only when `roomId` changes, and its comment says why widening that guard
is dangerous: "the same room emitting `scene_changed` is a token moving or a lid opening — follow,
do not settle, or the combat ceremony's pull-back never plays."

So a **targeted** path, not a wider guard: `Room` rebuilds its `Torches` group and `lighting.gd`
re-applies. Both calls already exist and are already driven from outside — `godot/dev/light_shots.gd`
does exactly `room._clear(room._ensure_group("Torches"))` then `room._build_wall_torches(size,
preset, burning)`. Re-entering a moved room later is a `roomId` change and picks up the new
lighting through the ordinary full rebuild for free.

## What the site must guarantee

Every room with fires declares a move, and **at least one room must move brighter** — or
`BRIGHTER` comes out of the design entirely. With 2-3 fills landing on whichever room the party is
standing in, a room that cannot move wastes a fill. And an unexercised direction is exactly what
AGENTS.md records as a *measured* failure rather than a worry: **a capability flag is a claim, not
a behaviour.**

The brighter direction is the half that was actually asked for — rising ALERT lighting the wall
sconces, "you're about to be discovered". It is what gives wall torches a role after `4h9.16`
empties the crypt of them. It costs `4h9.16`/`4h9.12`'s reasoning one room, once: a room that
lights up is a room the carried lantern is briefly redundant in, paid for with a patrol.

## Refused

- **LIGHT moving room fires.** LIGHT is the party's lamp. A clock that also blows out the room's
  fires is one clock meaning two things, and it spends the "one legible clock" the map settled and
  the fixed one-entry table that makes the greed decision computable.
- **Both directions drawn on one clock.** The dial would jitter with the draw. Direction is a
  property of the *place*, not of the roll.
- **A direction field walking the ladder.** It permits two steps, which contradicts one authored
  line per room and would put an ordering inside a closed enum.
- **Deriving direction from content** (has braziers -> darker, has brackets -> brighter). A claim,
  not a behaviour, and unreadable from the room file.
- **Putting the fire-move in the drawn consequence's bundle.** 0.6 moves per delve, and it buries
  a cross-cutting effect inside a table entry.
- **Making every fill spawn something** by dropping the table to three. The shape `ffi.2` refused
  by name.

## Not decided here

- **Whether a moved room stays moved between delves** — the campaign layer's. Moved to the map's
  Out of scope: M4 has no campaign layer and does not resume from a log.
- **Whether the change animates or snaps.** A build detail for `4h9.3`, and AGENTS.md's timebox
  says snap unless looking at it says otherwise.

title: The crypt is lit by its braziers, not by wall torches
description:
The crypt has ten orange wall torches and the fiction has never had any. Both recorded sessions
describe a chamber lit by two braziers and nothing else, and describe the fire as green:

  m2-twenty-turns: "braziers flank the chamber ahead, guttering low with green, smokeless flame
                    that turns every shadow bilious and sick"
  m3-traversal:    "a brazier burning low and green. It gives heat but no smoke."
  m3-traversal:    "the green braziers still hiss" -- and ten more references, treating it as
                    settled world fact across the whole session
  m3-traversal:    of the gallery, "choked with grey ash. Whatever burned here burned out a long
                    time before the green fires do"

This is the M2/M3 "the narrator can describe a world change nothing can back" family -- the copper
key, the hotdog, the breathing sarcophagus -- and it is the one instance where the board can back
it trivially, because the disagreement is a light count and a colour.

It also matters for M4 beyond dressing. A room full of wall fires makes a carried lantern
pointless. Taking the wall fires out of the crypt is what gives emberdelve-4h9.12's lantern
something to be the only light in.

WHAT TO CHANGE

1. The crypt stops being TORCHLIT. LightingPreset is a closed server-side enum (invariant 7) with
   content, a client-side TORCH_SPACING table in room.gd and test_room.gd hanging off it, so this
   is not a one-line edit. Decide whether the crypt takes an existing preset, a new one, or whether
   TORCHLIT's spacing goes to zero -- but do not confuse it with Room.Level, which room.gd:91 is
   emphatic is a separate axis.

2. The braziers burn green. Settled 2026-09-10 against the sheets, chosen against the floor rather
   than in isolation:

     flame light_color  Color(0.42, 0.86, 0.44)
     light_energy       2.8   (down from 4.5 -- green is where the eye is most sensitive, so the
                               orange number reads far hotter; the prose word is "guttering")
     Coals emission     the same colour lightened, replacing FLAME_CORE's warm cream

3. Re-pick Overlay.EXIT_TINT against the new floor. ADR-0011 records that the exit marker was
   first drawn amber against a floor it already matched and was invisible; the fix was cool
   markers -- EXIT_TINT is #3cd2c8, a teal -- chosen because the floor was warm. This change takes
   the warm floor away. The chosen green sits about 56 degrees of hue off the teal, which is why it
   was chosen over the colder candidates, but the marker still has to be looked at rather than
   assumed. AGENTS.md: "Anything that must read against these floors has to be picked against the
   floor, not in isolation."

HOW TO SEE IT

godot/dev/light_shots.gd renders the crypt through the real client at every combination of wall
fires and brazier colour, one contact sheet per camera corner. Run it before and after.

Not this ticket: which clock moves a room's fires in play. That is emberdelve-ffi.9.
acceptance_criteria: The crypt renders with no wall fires and two green braziers; the exit marker has been looked at against the new floor, not assumed; godot suite green.
notes:
**The crypt gains a `fires` object — emberdelve-ffi.9.**

Taking the wall fires out is this ticket. What the braziers *do* in play is ffi.9's, and it lands
in the same room file, so do them together or the crypt is edited twice:

    "fires": {
      "lit":   "<the green braziers, as authored>",
      "to":    "DARK",
      "moved": "<the night they finally go out>"
    }

`fires.lit` is the sentence that currently lives in `dmNotes.overview` — "Cold, close, and lit
green by two braziers that should have burned out centuries ago". **Move it out of `overview`**,
which becomes light-agnostic, so that exactly one fire line is true at any moment. `sensory`'s "The
braziers hiss" has the same problem and needs the same treatment or a rewrite that survives them
going out.

The crypt is the site's DARKER room. At least one room in emberdelve-4h9.8's site has to move
BRIGHTER instead, or that direction ships unexercised.
close_reason: The crypt is BRAZIERLIT, a new preset: TORCHLIT's Environment (the same resource, so the ambient of 0.7 stays one number) with TORCH_SPACING 0. DIM would have kept wall torches, DARK would have dropped the judged ambient to 0.35, and zeroing TORCHLIT would have made every generated TORCHLIT room an unlit void. No kit lists BRAZIERLIT, so it is authored-only. brazier.tscn burns Color(0.42,0.86,0.44) at 2.8, and its coals are that colour lightened by 0.45. The exit marker was checked on light_shots, which now draws it in every shot. On the green floor it is saturated teal, and reads better than it did under orange. It is occluded from corners 1 and 2 by the near wall, the same as before. Godot 247/247, server suite green. NOT done: the fires{lit,to,moved} object from the notes. It needs emberdelve-ffi.9's folded fire state, which is not built, so crypt.json's overview and sensory still carry the fire lines and the crypt will be edited again. Follow-up filed: emberdelve-4h9.17 (the gallery's cold brazier burns).

title: How a downed party member reads to the narrator
description:
## Question

How does a downed party member reach the DM prompt, and how does the narrator convey it
without counting?

Graduated from the map's fog list on 2026-09-09, when emberdelve-ffi.1 landed. Both that
ticket and emberdelve-4h9.13 hoped it would fold into the projection decision. It did not.

## Why it did not fold

ffi.1 settled that hurt reaches the prompt as a band, from `BeatRenderer.condition()`'s
existing four: barely marked / bloodied / badly hurt / barely standing. Every one of those
describes a creature **still on its feet**. Downed is not the bottom of that scale — it is a
different state, with a clock attached (emberdelve-4h9.13) and a delve riding on whether the
clock fills before the fight ends.

## What has to be decided

- Is downed a fifth band, or its own line in `## The party`? A fifth band keeps one
  vocabulary; a separate line admits it is a different kind of fact.
- Does the *downed clock* appear in the prompt at all? ffi.1 put LIGHT and ALERT in the block
  as bands. This clock is short, combat-scoped, and the tensest thing on the table. A band
  ("fading") may be right, or the fight block may own it, or the narrator may be told nothing
  and left to work from the beat.
- What `BeatRenderer` says on the blow that drops someone. Today `condition()` returns a band
  and a kill returns "is killed by the blow." Downed is neither.
- How the narrator conveys it. `dm.md` forbids reading hit points aloud and `## The fight`
  forbids stating them, so this is a hit point state that has to land as fiction. It is also
  the moment the player most needs to understand exactly what is true.
- Whether the party block's grammar survives a downed member at party size one. "Session
  state. It followed them in here and it will follow them out." reads oddly about someone on
  the floor.

## Watch for

The band vocabulary is shared with combat beats by ffi.1's decision — one wound vocabulary,
deliberately. Anything added here is added in both places or it is not added.
acceptance_criteria: A decision, as a resolution comment, on how downed reaches the DM prompt — band or its own line, whether its clock is carried, what BeatRenderer says on the blow that drops someone — and no number a narrator would read aloud.
close_reason: Out of scope: every decision it holds is downstream of the downed clock, which emberdelve-ffi.6 ruled out of M4.

comments.author: hampton.black
comments.text:
**Closed by emberdelve-ffi.6 — the question no longer exists.**

Every decision this ticket was opened to make is downstream of the downed clock, and ffi.6 ruled the
downed clock out of M4 (see emberdelve-4h9.13): 0 hit points is `PARTY_LOST`, immediately.

Taking its bullets in turn: there is no fifth band, because there is no state past `barely standing`
that a creature survives in. The downed clock does not appear in the prompt, because there is no
downed clock. `BeatRenderer` needs nothing new for the blow that drops someone — that blow is a kill,
and `condition()` already returns "is killed by the blow." The party block's grammar never meets a
downed member.

What remains of the concern — that the player most needs to understand exactly what is true at the
moment they lose — is owned by emberdelve-4h9.5, which ships `DelveEnded` with a `PARTY_LOST`
ending and replaces the client-side defeat check.

Ruled out of scope on the map rather than resolved: it is not a step on the route, it is a branch
the route no longer passes.

title: The projection carries the delve
description:
§15 names this as the expensive part of M4 and nothing in this epic owned it: "the projection work
that carries hurt, clock and objective state across a room boundary as fiction, which is the same
problem M3 is already inside."

The projection is the hand-built markdown block at `DmService.java:842` — `## The fight`,
`## Momentum`, `## Established`, `## Ways out`, `## Grid`. It never truncates, which is the whole
point of it against the six-turn transcript window, so everything added here is in every prompt for
the rest of the session.

What it has to carry after M4: hurt, the running clocks, whether the objective is held, and what
consumables remain.

**`## Ways out` is the cautionary tale and it is three weeks old.** The block listed doors and said
nothing about their state, so the model re-improvised the answer every turn — both 2026-09-07
sessions invented an ATHLETICS DC 20 to kick a door that was never shut, and one spent two turns on
a key against a lock that does not exist. A projection block that is vague about state is worse than
no block, because the model fills the gap and is then consistent about the wrong thing.

Two rules that are not negotiable:

- **Nothing here may produce a number the narrator would read aloud.** `dm.md` forbids reading hit
  points; the fight block forbids stating them; `AGENTS.md` says a wound is described, not counted,
  because "handing the model a fraction is an invitation to read it." emberdelve-pa8 records that
  `## Established` already leaks grid coordinates, and every block added is another surface for it.
- **Terse wins.** `AGENTS.md`: replacing the length rule with a seven-line explanation took narration
  from 514 to 654 characters; two blunt lines took it to 393. Measure before believing an edit
  helped.

## The form is decided — emberdelve-ffi.1, 2026-09-09

This ticket is the build. Do not re-decide any of it; the reasoning is in that ticket's
resolution comment.

- **One block, `## The party`, placed above `## Entities present` and below nothing.** Always
  present, never conditional — a conditional pressure block makes its *absence* information, and
  the model reads that absence as "no pressure" on the turn a clock starts running.
- **The party moves out of `## Entities present`.** That list holds two lifetimes once
  emberdelve-4h9.1 lands: session-scoped party, room-scoped hostiles rebuilt from room content.
  The block that survives a crossing must not be the one that gets rebuilt. It stays a list —
  invariant 2.
- **`DmService.java:797`'s `5/12 hp` goes.** It ships a fraction for every entity in both prompts
  today and no decision ever asked for it. It contradicts AGENTS.md and `BeatRenderer`.
- **Hurt is a band, from one shared source.** Extract `BeatRenderer.condition()`'s four —
  `barely marked` / `bloodied` / `badly hurt` / `barely standing` at 0.7 / 0.4 / 0.15 — and use
  the same function in both places. Not a second set of thresholds. A creature described one way
  in a beat and another way in the block above it is the copper-key failure in miniature.
- **`## Momentum` keeps its count.** The rule: *a count that drives a tool decision stays a count;
  a count that only describes state becomes a band.* Momentum feeds `dm-tools.md`'s two-failure
  escalation rule, and emberdelve-vy7 is what a vague version costs. Consumables keep their counts
  for the same reason — `use_item` takes one.
- **Both clocks, as bands, plus a fact-not-cue line.** LIGHT and ALERT. The line is not
  boilerplate: `## Secrets` proves this model narrates a thing into being when a block reads as a
  promise. The engine owns the dark. ALERT's band *vocabulary* is emberdelve-ffi.2's.
- **The objective gets a state line and a closed-world sentence.** The prop listing says where it
  is; it cannot say the party carries it out of a room the prop no longer belongs to.
- **All three consumable counters, always, zeroes included.** An omitted line is an invitation.
- **No new text in `dm.md` or `dm-tools.md`.** Facts in the projection, permissions in the prompts,
  nothing said twice. The fact-not-cue line inside the block is the only instruction added
  anywhere.
- **Grid coordinates stay on the party line.** `move_entity` needs bounds and adjacency;
  `dm.md:47` already forbids saying one aloud.

The exact wording of the block is in the resolution comment on emberdelve-ffi.1. Build that, then
measure — AGENTS.md's rule about believing an edit helped applies to this block as much as to the
length rule.

**Downed is not covered here** — emberdelve-ffi.8.
acceptance_criteria: Hurt, running clocks, whether the objective is held, and remaining consumables all reach the DM prompt in the form ffi.1 decided, and survive a room crossing. A test locks the headings and asserts no grid coordinate and no hit point fraction appears anywhere in the projection.
notes:
**A room's lighting is now folded state, and the projection has to say so — emberdelve-ffi.9.**

`DmService.worldState()` prints `## Room: <name>`, the authored `overview` and `sensory`, and
**never states the room's lighting**. That is a defect today, before any clock moves anything:
`crypt.json`'s overview is "Cold, close, and lit green by two braziers that should have burned out
centuries ago", so a room going dark leaves the DM describing green braziers over a dark board —
the copper key with its polarity reversed.

The room block prints the room's **current** fire line after `sensory`: `fires.lit` as authored,
`fires.moved` once the room has moved. Exactly one is true at a time, which is why the fire
sentence comes **out** of `overview` rather than being corrected by a later note. The wrong fix is
already in `crypt.json` — `dmNotes.theDoor`'s "do not restate it as though it still cannot open"
paragraph exists because the door's state changed and the authored prose could not. That is a
workaround for a schema that cannot vary; this one varies.

title: Downed is a clock, not a screen
description:
Today 0 hit points flips a screen on. Settled on the M4 map (emberdelve-ffi): 0 hit points drops you
and starts a short clock; if it fills before combat ends, the delve is lost.

Why a clock rather than the two obvious alternatives:

- **Instant death** makes the gate's own sentence false. §9 wants you "at 5 hit points and genuinely
  not know whether to open it" — at HP 12 against 1d6+2, five hit points is one bad roll from over,
  so the decision is not tense, it is already lost. A downed state widens the band where the
  question is live.
- **Death saves** are §6, and §15 puts the SRD engine in the next milestone with the content it
  adjudicates. A roll-per-turn here is the rules engine arriving early.
- **Recovering when the fight ends** is free at party size one: if you are the only combatant, the
  fight cannot end while you are down.

The clock is the primitive 4h9.3 builds anyway, at a scale it is already sized for, and the shape
stays correct when the party grows past one.

Segment count is emberdelve-ffi.6's answer.

Watch the narration: `dm.md` forbids reading hit points aloud and the fight block forbids stating
them, so downed is a hit point state the narrator has to convey without counting. **That did not
fold into emberdelve-ffi.1 as this ticket hoped** — ffi.1's band vocabulary bottoms out at "barely
standing", which is a creature still on its feet, and downed is a different state with a clock
attached. It graduated to emberdelve-ffi.8, which now blocks this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: 0 hit points emits a downed event and starts a clock rather than ending the delve. A test downs the player, ends the fight before the clock fills, and asserts they are up; a second lets it fill and asserts DelveEnded with PARTY_LOST. resolveAttack is unchanged in shape and nothing models a condition.
close_reason: Downed clock ruled out of M4 by emberdelve-ffi.6: isOver() ends the fight when the only player-controlled entity drops, so the clock is inert at party size one, and the 5-hp premise it rests on measured false. 0 hp is PARTY_LOST.

comments.author: hampton.black
comments.text:
**Closed by emberdelve-ffi.6 — the downed clock is ruled out of M4.**

Two of this ticket's three load-bearing claims are measurably false.

**"At HP 12 against 1d6+2, five hit points is one bad roll from over."** Measured: five hit points
against one goblin is a **72% survival**. Mean loss per goblin fight is 2.65 hp with a **median of
zero**. The fighter was never fragile.

**"Recovering when the fight ends is free at party size one: if you are the only combatant, the
fight cannot end while you are down."** `CombatEngine.isOver()` (line 147) returns true when no
living **player-controlled** entity remains. At party size one, dropping to 0 hp *ends the fight* —
so a clock resolved on "if it fills before combat ends" can never fill. The mechanism is inert by
construction, and the acceptance criterion here ("a test downs the player, ends the fight before the
clock fills, and asserts they are up") describes something that would pass trivially and always.

**0 hit points is `PARTY_LOST`, immediately.** The tension a downed state was meant to buy is
bought instead by the brute's doubt window — 4-10 hit points, 45.7% survival at exactly 5 — and
bought *before* the door rather than after the drop, which is where §9 puts the decision.

The "not a screen" half is already owned by emberdelve-4h9.5: `godot/chrome/defeat.gd`'s
client-side `hp <= 0` check on a hardcoded `"fighter"` goes with `DelveEnded`.

Re-enters with a second party member, or with §6's death saves in the milestone that brings the SRD
engine. Not deleted — the reasoning is the point.

title: The party carries a light, and the clock is its fuel
description:
The party carries no light. `room.gd:315` builds wall torches from the room's own `LightingPreset`,
capped by a per-room `MAX_TORCH_LIGHTS` budget, and `Room.Level` is a separate axis the file is
emphatic about not confusing with it. So the LIGHT clock §9 names first has nothing to burn down.

Settled on the M4 map (emberdelve-ffi): light moves to the party. A carried lantern, fuelled by the
LIGHT clock, read as a shrinking radius. Room torches stay room-owned so `Level.DIM` keeps its one
meaning — the "one meaning per colour" rule the health bar already taught this project.

The `torch` consumable refuels it. §9's Consumable enum is already potion / torch / rope, so this
links 4h9.2's counter map to 4h9.3's clock and states the greed loop in one line: how deep you go is
how many torches you brought.

**The server ships the radius; the client never derives it** (invariant 1), for the same reason
`SceneState.blocked` and `CombatView.legalMoves` are shipped rather than computed. A client that
picked its own radius would render a replayed session differently from the session.

The 2026-09-07 playtest recorded that invented lanterns already travel with the party as facts with
no prop behind them, and `kaykit_halloween` ships an unused `lantern_standing`. This is the hotdog
problem solved the cheap way round: give the board the thing the fiction keeps inventing.

Object model is emberdelve-ffi.3; how the radius reads is emberdelve-ffi.5. This ticket is the
build.
acceptance_criteria: The party carries a light whose fuel is the LIGHT clock, folded from events. The server ships the radius; the client never derives it. Spending a torch refuels it. A test fills the clock and asserts the light state changes; a second spends a torch and asserts it recovers. Room torches and MAX_TORCH_LIGHTS are untouched.
notes:
**Settled by emberdelve-ffi.6: a torch resets the LIGHT clock to empty**, rather than adding a
fixed number of segments. LIGHT is 6 segments and **the party starts with 2 torches**, so the whole
light budget of a delve is 18 ticks.

Against that: a careful five-room delve is about 9 ticks, a greedy one about 15. Comfortable, then
tight -- the greed decision stated in torches.

The tick rule that makes the radius mean something: **every room entry ticks, including a room
already visited**, so going one room deeper costs two segments, one in and one out. See
emberdelve-4h9.3, which also carries the reversal on what a failed check does (nothing; a natural 1
ticks one).

Numbers and method: `docs/evidence/m4-attrition-sim.py`.
---

**2026-09-10.** Two things moved under this ticket.

`EnvTorchlit`'s ambient is now **0.7**, not 1.1 (emberdelve-27l). That was the number lifting the
surfaces a shrinking radius has to leave, so the radius is now judgeable. Carried forward from that
resolution: 0.7 still shows the whole room's layout, so it is right for a torchlit room and
probably still too high for a room the lantern is the only light in — `EnvDark`'s 0.35 is the
territory to look at. emberdelve-ffi.5 owns that.

The crypt loses its wall fires (emberdelve-4h9.16), which is what gives the lantern something to be
the only light in. Whether the LIGHT clock also moves the *room's* fires is open —
emberdelve-ffi.9, and it decides whether a torch that resets LIGHT also relights what went out.
---

**emberdelve-ffi.9 resolved: a torch relights nothing.** A torch is the party's; the fires are the
room's. The LIGHT clock does not touch room fires at all — the dial lives on ALERT, moves the
party's current room one step in the direction that room authored, and ratchets, so a room that has
moved stays moved for the delve.

One cost to know about: a room that moves **BRIGHTER** is a room the carried lantern is briefly
redundant in. That is one room, once per delve at most, and it is paid for with whatever the ALERT
fill also drew.

---

**emberdelve-ffi.3 resolved 2026-09-10: it is a torch, and as an object it is nothing new.**

**Not a lantern.** §9 already calls it a torch (`docs/ai-dm-system-design.md:612` — "it never
decides that the torch went out"), a torch is not lantern fuel, and `kaykit_dungeon` ships the
handheld pair `torch.gltf` / `torch_lit.gltf` — distinct from the `torch_mounted` bracket
`room.gd:352` puts on walls. `kaykit_halloween`'s `lantern_standing` is floor dressing, not
something a figure holds. Reserve **wall torch** for the room's fixture in prose and test names.

**No new folded state.** The party's light is a pure function of the LIGHT clock. No `Lantern`
record, no field on `PartyMember`, no new event. Not a `Prop` either: `Prop` carries `x, y` in a
room, `Diff` has no `PropMoved`, and `reveal_prop`'s closed per-room enum would swallow it.

**What ships:** a closed `PartyLight` on `SceneState`, plus a `Diff` for mid-turn changes.

| `PartyLight` | LIGHT segments (of 6) |
|---|---|
| `FULL` | 0-1 |
| `LOW` | 2-3 |
| `GUTTERING` | 4 |
| `FAILING` | 5 |
| `OUT` | 6 |

The five names are `emberdelve-ffi.2`'s own sign names, so what the DM narrates and what the player
sees are the same five words. **The level is level-triggered; signs stay edge-triggered** — spending
a torch at `FAILING` puts the pool back to `FULL` and fires nothing on the way down.

**Not the segment count** (the wire must be unable to carry the counter that must never be drawn)
and **not a radius in world units** (appearance numbers live on the client, the way `TORCH_ENERGY`
and the ambient do; what the server owns is how much light there is). If `emberdelve-ffi.5` gives the
pool mechanical teeth, the server ships a **square list** alongside, the way `SceneState.blocked`
does — it does not turn the level into a number.

**Where the nodes go — split them.**

- **Light:** one `OmniLight3D` owned by `World`, a sibling of `Tokens`, positioned each frame at the
  centroid of living player-controlled tokens. `world.gd:40` already runs `_process` and
  `token.position` is tweened in the same frame, so it follows exactly. Three reasons it cannot live
  anywhere else: `MAX_TORCH_LIGHTS` is a per-`Room` budget (`room.gd:313`); `world.gd:277`
  `_rebuild_tokens()` frees and rebuilds every token on a room change; and invariant 2 — the light is
  the party's, not a member's.
- **Mesh:** `torch` / `torch_lit` on a `BoneAttachment3D` at `handslot.l`. `Knight.glb` has
  `handslot.l` and `handslot.r` as skin joints, animated by every stolen clip, and its mesh list is
  nine body parts with no weapon. **Add it after `_fit()` and `_self_lit()` have run** — otherwise it
  perturbs the bounding box the height calibration is measured from and gets its materials rewritten.
- **Not a bone-attached light.** `handslot.l` swings with `Melee_1H_Attack_Chop`; the pool must not.

**The cycle.** The party walks in **holding a lit torch** — `emberdelve-ffi.6`'s 18-tick budget is
6 + 6 + 6, so the clock starts empty with one torch already burning and two spares. At `OUT` the mesh
**swaps to the unlit `torch`, it never comes off**: a hand that empties reads as the torch being
dropped, which did not happen. Two mesh states only; everything continuous is `emberdelve-ffi.5`.

**Out with none left is not a sixth value.** `PartyLight` describes light, the count describes supply.
`LIGHT_OUT`'s directive register takes a second clause when the count is zero — *your last torch* —
chosen server-side from state that already exists.

**Never a pick target** (`ADR-0011`, and `emberdelve-7m6`'s `brazier-east` lesson with a mesh that
moves every turn). The torch is spent from an **exploration action bar** instead — see
`emberdelve-4h9.2` and `emberdelve-4h9.11`. Refused at exactly zero segments, where it would reset
nothing; spending at `LOW` wastes two segments and stays legal, because that is the greed decision.

**A relight latches a directive** on the rail — one clause, no model call. Not because the player
misses the moment, but because the projection would otherwise say the light is full again with
nothing to say why, and the narrator reconciles that afresh every turn. The rail itself is
single-slot today and needs fixing first: `emberdelve-4h9.3`.

title: Rest — the pressure valve
description:
Nothing in this epic builds a rest, and §9 requires one: "Healing is scarce, and rests are a clock
tick rather than a free reset." 4h9.3 names rests as a tick trigger and stops there; 4h9.2 covers
potions. The server contains no rest and no healing of any kind today.

Settled on the M4 map (emberdelve-ffi):

- An explicit player action, not something the narrator can grant. §9 is blunt about why — "the
  model always says yes", and the engine is the only thing here that can make something scarce.
- Legal only in a room with no living hostile in it. An engine rule, one line, not authored content
  — a content-marked safe room would not survive contact with generated rooms next milestone.
- Ticks every running clock one segment.
- Restores a fixed small amount. Not a roll: the dice are for questions the DM is about to answer,
  and "how much did you recover" is not a moment. Fixed and small keeps the arithmetic in the
  player's head, which is where the tension lives.

The rest is the pressure valve that makes the clock legible — you spend a segment on purpose and
watch it fill. Without it, "go deeper or get out" is a binary the player makes once.

Event and fold like everything else (invariant 8). Mechanics-phase tool, not reconcile: a false
positive spends clock segments the player did not agree to.

The amount, and how hard a rest ticks, are emberdelve-ffi.6's answer, not this ticket's.
acceptance_criteria: Rest is a mechanics-phase tool, validated server-side, rejected in a room holding a living hostile. It emits an event; the restoration and every clock tick fold from it. A scripted test rests, asserts hit points up and every clock advanced by one, with no model in the path. The narrator cannot grant a rest by describing one.
notes:
**A rest restores 4 hit points** -- settled by emberdelve-ffi.6. A fifth of the 20-point bar.

Chosen for legibility, not balance, and the sim says so plainly: across a whole delve a 3-point
rest and an 8-point rest differ by under 1.5%, because the fights dominate. So the number should be
one a player can hold in their head while deciding whether a segment is worth it. A potion restores
8 (emberdelve-4h9.2) -- deliberately twice a rest, because being visibly stronger than the free
option is what justifies it being finite.

Ticking stays as settled: one segment on every running clock.

Numbers and method: `docs/evidence/m4-attrition-sim.py`.

---

**emberdelve-ffi.3 resolved 2026-09-10: rest is a button, and its gate is a hint on the client and a
rule on the server.**

Rest joins torch and potion on an **exploration action bar** — a sibling of `combat_bar.gd`, not an
extension of `party_badge.gd`. The principle that puts it there: **a button per player action the DM
does not adjudicate.** A fixed 4 points and one segment on every running clock is no more a question
than `enterExit` is. See `emberdelve-4h9.2` for the full argument and for why this amends "no UI
beyond a count" rather than breaching it.

**The gate is not `mode == EXPLORATION`.** `emberdelve-ffi.2`'s `Disposition.WARY` puts a living
hostile on the board in exploration mode, and you cannot rest while it watches you. The rule stays
what this ticket already says — no living hostile in the room — and the client reads living hostiles
from `Table.scene.entities`, which is already shipped and already current-room-scoped.

**The server refuses; the button greys as a hint.** That is `SceneState.blocked`'s own stated rule:
"The server refuses the move either way; this is the hint, not the rule." The button saying so a
moment earlier does not make the client own the rule.

**Exploration-only, and that is measured rather than chosen.** `docs/evidence/m4-attrition-sim.py:60`
— `fight()` heals nobody, and every rest in `delve()` happens between rooms. `emberdelve-ffi.6`'s
doubt window was tuned with no in-combat recovery in it.

Buttons key off `Table.awaiting_dm`, so the bar goes dead while the DM is speaking, like
`debug_bar.gd:41` and `combat_bar.gd:255`.

title: Write the M4 design spec
description:
## Question

Write the M4 design spec.

`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-XX-m4-delve-design.md`, in the shape of
`2026-09-05-m3-traversal-design.md` and `2026-08-23-m2-spine-design.md`.

This is the map's destination. It is written in **one pass at the end**, from the map's Settled
block and the resolution comments on every closed ticket — deliberately, because M1/M2/M3's specs
read as documents with an argument, and a case written in eight sittings by eight agents is not one.

## What goes in it

The map's `## Settled at charting` block is the raw material for most of it; each closed ticket's
resolution comment is the rest. The spec should make the *argument*, not minute the decisions —
where §9 was a bet, say what play and design have since settled and why.

Specifically it has to carry:

- The delve as a state with an ending, and why `Ending` is descriptive rather than a verdict.
- Attrition: the light clock, the carried lantern, the torch that refuels it, rest, and downed.
- What the engine owns and what the narrator owns, restated for the clock — §9's "it never decides
  that the torch went out" is the sentence the whole section hangs on.
- The projection, per emberdelve-ffi.1.
- What M4 deliberately does not build, and the re-entry condition for each.
- What this milestone hands the generator, since M1's outstanding half comes next and 4h9.8 is
  already collecting the list.

## After it is signed

Update `AGENTS.md` — the milestone table, the shortcuts table (the two-room shortcut and the
"do not add a third room" anti-goal are retired by 4h9.8), and the LLM tools list if `use_item` or
anything else lands. `AGENTS.md` is the operational file and it wins where it and the design doc
disagree, so it cannot lag.

Amend `docs/ai-dm-system-design.md` §2a with whatever M4 reversed. Every milestone so far has
reversed something; §9 was written expecting to.

`CONTEXT.md` gains the delve vocabulary — delve, clock, sign, consequence, objective, rest, downed.
It is a glossary and not a second rules file.
acceptance_criteria: The spec exists, reads as a document with an argument rather than minutes, and carries the delve as a state with an ending, attrition, the engine/narrator line for the clock, the projection, what M4 does not build, and what it hands the generator. AGENTS.md, design doc 2a and CONTEXT.md updated.

title: The numbers — tune attrition until 5 hit points is a real decision
description:
## Question

What are the numbers, such that standing in front of a door at 5 hit points is a real state?

§9's gate is stated as something to feel: "you should be able to stand in front of a door at 5 hit
points and genuinely not know whether to open it." That is an arithmetic claim as much as a design
one, and today's numbers do not support it.

## Why today's numbers fail the gate

`AGENTS.md` shortcuts: Fighter AC 16, HP 12; Goblin +4 to hit, 1d6+2 damage. At HP 12 against
1d6+2, five hit points is one bad roll from over. The decision at that door is not tense — it is
already lost, and a player who understands the numbers knows it. The band in which the gate's
question is live has to be wide enough to stand in.

This is a `--demo` job. `ScriptedDiceRoller` exists for exactly this: reproducible tuning runs with
no model in the path.

## What has to be decided

- **Party hit points**, and whether the fighter's 12 moves.
- **The rest's restoration.** Settled: a fixed small amount, no roll. What amount.
- **Clock segment counts** — LIGHT, ALERT, and the downed clock. §9's record has `segments` as a
  field precisely so this is a number and not a constant.
- **How many torches the party starts with**, which is the greed loop's actual dial: how deep you go
  is how many torches you brought.
- **Potion count**, same reasoning.
- **How hard a rest ticks.** Settled at one segment per clock; whether that survives contact with a
  4-5 room site is what this ticket measures.
- **Whether the goblin's damage moves**, and what a second stat block (4h9.9) is worth in the same
  arithmetic.

## The shape of the answer

A delve of 4-5 rooms in which a careful player reaches the objective with resources left, a greedy
one is genuinely in danger going deeper, and the light clock can fill before the site is exhausted.
Stated as numbers, with the scripted run that produced them.

## Constraint

Do not build a rules engine to get there. The forty lines of `CombatEngine.resolveAttack` are the
anti-goal's own example, and every dial named above is a content or config number.
acceptance_criteria: Numbers for party hit points, rest restoration, every clock's segments, starting torches and potions, stated with the --demo run that produced them. A careful delve leaves resources spare; a greedy one is genuinely in danger; the light clock can fill before the site is exhausted.
close_reason: Resolved: fighter HP 20, goblin weakened to AC12/HP6/+3/1d4+1, new brute AC13/HP16/+4/1d8+2 landing the doubt window on 4-10 with 45.7% survival at exactly 5 hp. Rest 4, potion 8, LIGHT and ALERT 6 segments, 2 torches, 2 potions, 5-room site. Two charting reversals: failed checks no longer tick LIGHT (nat 1 only), and the downed clock is dropped.

comments.author: hampton.black
comments.text:
## Resolved

Every number below comes from `docs/evidence/m4-attrition-sim.py`, seeded, which mirrors
`CombatEngine.resolveAttack` and `GoblinAi` exactly — natural 20 auto-hits and doubles the damage
dice only, natural 1 auto-misses, initiative ties go to the goblin's DEX +2, and a creature that
starts away from its foe spends its first turn closing.

**This ticket could not be the `--demo` job it was filed as.** `ScriptedDiceRoller` gives
reproducible dice, but there is no delve loop to run them through — no clock, no rest, no site. The
reproducible artifact is the simulator instead, committed so every figure in the spec can be
re-derived.

### The ticket's premise was wrong, and wrong in the informative direction

It said that at HP 12 against 1d6+2, five hit points is "one bad roll from over". Measured, it is a
**72% survival**. A single goblin costs a mean of 2.65 hp, a **median of zero**, and drops the
fighter 8.6% of the time. The fighter was never fragile; the goblin was never a threat.

Worse, and this is the finding the whole resolution turns on: **hit points barely inform the
decision at all.** 1 hp survives 65%, 5 hp survives 72%, 12 hp survives 91%. What kills you is
whether the goblin connects, not what you had left. The number §9 asks the player to agonise over
was not carrying information.

### The doubt window, and the two dials that set it

The **doubt window** is the run of hit points where P(surviving the next room) is between 40% and
70% — where the gate's sentence is literally true. It has two independent owners, and conflating
them is what made this ticket hard to start:

- **The encounter sets where the window sits.** Max HP does not move it: HP 20 and HP 24 against
  two goblins have the *identical* window, 8–16.
- **Max HP sets how much bar there is above the window** — the run-up. At HP 12 the brute's window
  (4–10) is more than half the bar, so the player is in coin-flip territory from the first fight
  and the delve has no early phase to spend.

Today's window is **1–4 hp, four points wide, sitting below the number the gate names.**

### Party size stays at one

A second body collapses the danger by fourteen times — party of 1 versus two goblins wipes 42.8%,
party of 2 wipes 3.1%. Invariant #2's `List<PartyMember>` keeps the door open at no cost. M4's gate
is about attrition, not party tactics.

### The action economy inverts the obvious encounter ladder

Against a party of one, **N weak enemies is always harder than one strong enemy**, because each of
them takes a full turn while the fighter takes one. Dropped-from-full at HP 12: one brute 23.7%,
two goblins 43.2%, three goblins 79.9%. "A few weak mobs" cannot be the easy fight while the goblin
is AC 15 / HP 7 / 1d6+2.

### The numbers

| | Was | Is | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fighter max HP | 12 | **20** | Buys the run-up above the doubt window. The delve-length dial; nothing else does that job. |
| Goblin | AC 15, HP 7, +4, 1d6+2 | **AC 12, HP 6, +3, 1d4+1** | Weakened so packs can be the *easy* fight. HP 6 keeps it at 75% one-shot on a hit — usually one blow, sometimes two. HP 4 or 5 dies to every hit, which makes a pack a formality. |
| Brute (new, 4h9.9) | — | **AC 13, HP 16, +4, 1d8+2** | Lands the doubt window on **4–10, 50% at 6 hp, 45.7% survival at exactly 5**. Drops a full-health fighter only 8.2% of the time: a fight you almost never lose fresh and genuinely might lose hurt. |
| Rest restores | — | **4** | A fifth of the bar. |
| Potion restores | — | **8** | Two fifths — visibly worth more than the free option, which is what justifies it being finite. |
| LIGHT segments | — | **6** | |
| ALERT segments | — | **6** | Signs at 2 / 4 / 5, as `emberdelve-ffi.2` wrote them. |
| Starting torches | — | **2** | An 18-tick light budget against a careful delve's ~9 and a greedy delve's ~15. |
| Starting potions | — | **2** | |
| Site | — | **5 rooms, ~3 holding a fight** | Objective shallow; two rooms of optional depth, which is where the greed decision lives. |

**The rest and potion figures were chosen for legibility, not balance.** A 3-point rest and an
8-point rest differ by under 1.5% across a whole delve — the fights dominate completely. Round
fractions of the bar are worth more than a tuned number nobody can hold in their head.

### The encounter ladder, against fighter HP 20

| Encounter | Dropped from full | 50% at | Doubt window | Survives at 5 hp |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 mobs | 1.3% | 3 hp | 1–5 | 63.3% |
| 1 brute | 8.2% | 6 hp | 4–10 | **45.7%** |
| 3 mobs | 12.0% | 9 hp | 8–13 | 27.5% |
| brute + 2 mobs | 52.7% | 20 hp | 18–20 | 5.8% |

Two shapes land on comparable weight — one brute and three mobs — which is the variety the site
wants without a difficulty cliff. **brute + 2 mobs is not a designed room**; it is what the ALERT
clock does to you.

### The whole delve

| | Lost | HP left | Items unspent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Careful — 3 fights, objective, out | **26.1%** | 10.8 / 20 | 2.51 |
| Greedy — 5 fights, two rooms deeper | **77.1%** | 7.7 / 20 | 0.98 |

Stated honestly: the careful figure assumes the player **fights everything they meet and never
avoids anything.** Avoidance is what the ALERT signs are for, and a player who reads them should sit
below 26%. It is not tuned lower to look better.

Note what this interacts with: **exits are illegal in combat** (locked at M2, no fleeing). Every
fight is to the death. So the greed decision is "do I open this door", never "do I finish this
fight" — which is exactly why the danger has to be legible *before* the door, and exactly what the
ALERT signs are for.

### The light budget, and why depth costs two

LIGHT ticks on every room entry, every rest, and every natural 1. **Every room entry ticks,
including a room already visited** — the lantern does not care that you have been here. So **going
one room deeper costs two segments, one in and one out**, which is what turns depth from vaguely
risky into computable. A torch resets LIGHT to empty. A careful five-room delve is ~9 ticks; a
greedy one ~15; two torches plus the starting fill is 18.

## Two decisions settled at charting that do not survive contact

### The failed-check tick hands the scarcity budget to the model

Counted in the recorded sessions. `session-m2-twenty-turns.jsonl`: 20 checks, **14 failures**, 3
natural 1s. `session-m3-traversal.jsonl`: 11 checks, **2 failures**, none natural. Same game, same
player — a sevenfold difference in fill rate, because M2's DM reached for DC 15–25 and M3's reached
for DC 5–10.

A LIGHT clock fed by that has its fill rate set by the narrator's taste in difficulty. That is the
opposite of `emberdelve-ffi.2`'s reason for making LIGHT predictable, and it hands scarcity to the
one component §9 says must never own it: *"the engine is the only thing in this system that can
make something scarce."*

**Reversed: a natural 1 ticks LIGHT one segment; an ordinary failed check ticks nothing.** The play
observation that motivated the original rule survives intact — the dropped lantern on a 1 is still
an engine tick, a fired table and a narrated event. It lands once or twice a delve. Charting
rejected nat-1-alone as "too rare to build pressure", but that was judged against
failed-check-alone; the room tick carries the pressure, and it is fully player-controlled.

### The downed clock cannot fill

`CombatEngine.isOver()` (line 147) returns true when no living **player-controlled** entity remains.
At party size one, dropping to 0 hp *ends the fight* — so a clock resolved on "if it fills before
combat ends" is inert by construction. `emberdelve-4h9.13` states the opposite in its own body
("the fight cannot end while you are down"), and it also rests on the 5-hp premise this ticket
measured false.

**Reversed: 0 hit points is `PARTY_LOST`, immediately.** The tension the downed clock was meant to
buy is already bought by the brute's 4–10 window, and bought *before* the door rather than after the
drop, which is where §9 puts the decision. `emberdelve-4h9.13` is closed and the downed clock is
ruled out of M4; it re-enters with a second party member or with §6's death saves.

## Build consequences

- **`CombatEngineTest` builds through `ContentLoader`**, so it reads the real `fighter.json` and
  `goblin.json`. Changing either moves every scripted-dice fixture in it — the faces are chosen
  against AC 15 and 7 hp. Real work, flagged on `emberdelve-4h9.9`, not a content-only edit.
- **Recorded logs are unaffected.** `EntitySpawned` carries the whole `Entity`, so a replayed
  session uses the stats it was written with. No schema bump, no re-record.
- **`AGENTS.md`'s shortcuts table becomes untrue the moment this lands** — the Fighter and Goblin
  rows both. It is deliberately not edited now: this map plans, and a rules file describing a build
  that has not happened is worse than one that is merely out of date.

comments.author: hampton.black
comments.text:
The reversal on what ticks LIGHT is recorded as [ADR-0013](docs/adr/0013-scarcity-is-the-engines-not-the-narrators.md), *Scarcity is the engine's, not the narrator's* — the general rule behind it, which is that no engine resource may be spent as a consequence of a value the model selected. The failed-check tick looked engine-owned because every line of it was server-side; what leaked was that `roll_check`'s difficulty enum, closed and validated exactly as invariant #7 requires, still lets the model choose the failure rate and therefore the burn rate.

The numbers themselves stay here rather than in the ADR: they are content, they will move when the site is authored, and the spec is written from the resolution comments.

title: How the shrinking light radius reads
description:
## Question

How does the shrinking light radius read?

Call the `prototype` skill. Settled at charting: the party carries a lantern, the LIGHT clock is its
fuel, and radius is the read — the pool of light shrinks as the clock fills. Radius was chosen over
colour-and-flicker because it changes what the player can *do*: less visible floor is less floor to
click, so the clock has mechanical teeth without the engine growing a visibility rule.

That is the decision. This ticket is the judgement, and it is a judgement made by looking.

## What has to be decided

- The radius at full and at empty, and the curve between them.
- Whether the falloff is soft or hard, and whether the edge is a place the player reads as a
  boundary or as atmosphere.
- Whether anything else moves with it — colour, flicker rate, the shadow behaviour of the room's own
  torches at the edge of the pool.
- What "less floor to click" actually means mechanically, or whether it stays purely visual for M4.
  Note this is the expensive branch: a real visibility rule is server-owned under invariant 1, the
  way `SceneState.blocked` and `legalMoves` are, and it is not obviously in scope.

## Two things that will waste the session if forgotten

**Turn off the editor's Preview Sun and Preview Environment.** They are on by default and stack on
top of whatever environment a tool scene adds, so the room reads far brighter than the game. From
the 4h9.10 spike notes: every appearance decision made under them is made under the wrong light.

**The anti-goal is real.** `AGENTS.md`: "Do not tune lighting and post-processing for more than one
evening. Timebox it. This is the single largest time sink in the project and it will consume as
much as you give it."

## Blocked on

- emberdelve-27l — at ambient 1.1 a shrinking radius will not read at all.
- emberdelve-ffi.3 — the prototype needs a thing to shrink, and where the light node lives is that
  ticket's answer.
acceptance_criteria: A radius at full and at empty, a falloff, and a screenshot of each judged with Preview Sun and Preview Environment OFF. A stated answer on whether the shrinking pool is visual only in M4. Timeboxed to one evening.
notes:
**Unblocked by emberdelve-ffi.3, 2026-09-10. Here is the thing to shrink.**

It is a **torch**, not a lantern — `docs/ai-dm-system-design.md:612` calls it one, and
`kaykit_dungeon` ships the handheld pair `torch.gltf` / `torch_lit.gltf`.

**The light node:** one `OmniLight3D` owned by `World`, a sibling of `Tokens`, positioned each frame
at the centroid of living player-controlled tokens. It is deliberately **not** under a `Room`
(`MAX_TORCH_LIGHTS` is a per-room budget, `room.gd:313`) and **not** on a token (`world.gd:277`
`_rebuild_tokens()` frees every token on a room change) and **not** on the hand bone (`handslot.l`
swings with `Melee_1H_Attack_Chop`; the pool must not lurch with a sword stroke).

**What the server ships is a level, not a radius** — a closed five-value `PartyLight`:

| `PartyLight` | LIGHT segments (of 6) |
|---|---|
| `FULL` | 0-1 |
| `LOW` | 2-3 |
| `GUTTERING` | 4 |
| `FAILING` | 5 |
| `OUT` | 6 |

**So the metres are yours.** Radius, falloff, energy and colour per level live on the client, the way
`TORCH_ENERGY`, `TORCH_RANGE` and the ambient `emberdelve-27l` moved already do — a look tuned by
looking, not by recompiling the server. What is server-owned is how much light there is, because that
folds from the log and must replay.

`OUT` is not black. The room's own fires may still be burning (`emberdelve-ffi.9`) and the ambient
still lifts the floor; the sting is a `DARK` room at `OUT`, which is where `EnvDark`'s 0.35 territory
gets judged.

**The mesh is two states only** — `torch_lit` from `FULL` through `FAILING`, `torch` at `OUT`.
Everything continuous is yours: flame scale, flicker rate, whether the head dims as it gutters.

**On the expensive branch.** If the shrinking pool gets mechanical teeth — less visible floor meaning
less clickable floor — the server ships a **square list** alongside the level, the way
`SceneState.blocked` and `CombatView.legalMoves` already are. It does not turn the level into a
number, and the client still derives nothing.

title: How the end of a delve reads on screen
description:
## Question

How does the end of a delve read on screen?

Call the `prototype` skill. This is a "how should it look" question and the cheapest way to answer
it is a rough artifact to react to.

## What exists

`godot/chrome/defeat.gd` and the `Overlay/Defeat` node in `chrome.tscn` — a veil, a line of text,
and a Restart button. It survived the Godot migration intact. Its docstring carries the finding
that produced it: "A dead player character used to be only a dropped token: combat ended, the mode
pill flipped back, and nothing said what had happened. With the input box refusing text and the
board refusing clicks, that reads as a crash rather than a death."

It is also the thing being replaced. It decides the run is over client-side, from
`Table.entity("fighter")` with `hp <= 0` hardcoded — it cannot distinguish three endings, and it
names a singleton player against invariant 2. The delve ending becomes a `DelveEnded` event and the
client renders what it is told.

## What has to be decided

- **What "what was spent" actually shows.** 4h9.5 says the sting is in what was spent — rooms
  entered, potions drunk, what was carried, what was left behind. Which of those earn a line, and
  whether a number or a phrase.
- **Whether the DM narrates it.** 4h9.5: "That is a read of state, not a narration call, though a
  narration call over it is cheap and probably right." A narration call here is the last thing the
  player hears, which is either the best place in the game for one or the worst place to be
  waiting. Note `openScene` measures 515-712ms to first token, 1.8-3.1s total, for a comparable
  single-phase prose call.
- **Whether the three endings share one screen.** Extracting with the objective and being wiped are
  the same *moment* structurally and completely different emotionally.
- **What the way on is.** Restart today throws the session away. `GameEngine.restart()` reuses the
  original `SessionStarted` header, so under `--demo` a restarted delve is the *same* delve, same
  seed. That is a gift for tuning and a problem for a player who just lost.
- **Whether the board stays visible behind it.** The veil hides what happened; the loss is on the
  board.

## Constraint

Only `PARTY_LOST` is losing (settled at charting). Extracting empty-handed is a legitimate cautious
outcome and the screen must not read as a scolding — §9's greed decision only works if leaving
early is respectable.
acceptance_criteria: A rough artifact linked from this ticket, and a decision on what the ending shows for each of the three endings, whether the DM narrates it, and what the way on is.

title: What the carried lantern is, as an object
description:
## Question

What is the carried lantern, as an object?

Settled at charting: light moves from the room to the party. `room.gd:315` builds wall torches from
the room's own `LightingPreset`, and `Room.Level` is a separate axis the file is emphatic about not
confusing with it — so a LIGHT clock has nothing to burn down unless the party carries something.

That decision leaves the object model open, and it touches three things that already exist.

## What has to be decided

- **Is it a `Prop`?** Props have an id, a closed `PropType`, `hidden`, and live in a room. A carried
  light lives on the party and moves with it. That is either a new kind of thing or a stretch of an
  existing one.
- **Is it a token attachment?** `godot/world/tokens/token.gd` mounts meshes on a skinned figure;
  `kaykit_halloween` ships an unused `lantern_standing`. Whether the light is visibly *held* is a
  separate question from where its state lives.
- **How does it interact with picking?** emberdelve-7m6 is the open question of which props become
  pick targets, and ADR-0011 (visible is not addressable) is the rule. A lantern the player can
  click is a lantern they can put down, which is a mechanic nobody asked for.
- **Where does the light source node live?** Not in `Room` — `MAX_TORCH_LIGHTS` is deliberately a
  per-room budget and the carried light must not spend it. Probably on the party token or on
  `World`, and that decision constrains the radius work.
- **What happens when it goes out?** The lantern presumably still exists at zero fuel. Whether
  relighting is a `use_item` on a torch, or something else, is the seam between this and 4h9.2.

## Why this is worth deciding before the radius is prototyped

The prototype needs a thing to shrink. Deciding the look first and the object afterwards is how the
renderer ends up owning state (invariant 1) — and the server must ship the radius, not derive it
client-side, for the same reason `SceneState.blocked` is shipped rather than computed.

## Prior art worth reading first

The 2026-09-07 playtest recorded that invented lanterns already travel with the party as facts with
no prop behind them. The fiction reached for this object before the engine had it.

close_reason: It is a torch, not a lantern, and as an object it is nothing new: the party's light is a pure function of the LIGHT clock, shipped as a closed five-value PartyLight enum whose names are ffi.2's own sign names. The light node is World-owned and follows the party; the mesh rides handslot.l. Never a pick target — instead an exploration action bar carries torch, potion and rest, all exploration-only because the attrition tuning was measured with no in-combat healing. Surfaced that the directive rail is single-slot with five writers incoming; filed on 4h9.3. Crossing narration graduated to its own ticket.
