title: Keep picking and the camera on the room the party is in
description:
Two consequences of the current room no longer sitting at the world origin.

PICKING. world_to_grid still assumes the live room is centred on the origin, so
it silently mis-resolves the moment origins are entrance-anchored. Make it
room-aware — the exact inverse of grid_to_world for a given room — and have
pick_at resolve which room a floor hit landed in. A hit outside the current
room's rectangle returns null: a DIM room is scenery and a click in one must not
issue a move.

_target_under needs no change for this epic. It scans Room/Walls, and the door
back is in the current room's own wall run, so chaining crossings already works.
Neighbour walls live under a different holder and are never scanned, so a DIM
room cannot steal a pick.

CAMERA. Two places assume the origin is the current room's centre:
_framing_target() centres combat framing on Vector3.ZERO, and _clamp_to_room()
builds its clamp corners at +/- extent around the origin. Left alone, standing in
the gallery clamps the camera to a rectangle around the crypt while it tries to
follow a party in the gallery — which is exactly the failure camera_rig.gd:23
warns about, "clamp-to-room quietly cancels the follow". Translate both to the
current room's origin.
design:
Clamp to the current room's rectangle rather than the discovered bounding box.
The bounding box would let the camera drift a long way from the party in a large
dungeon, and _combat_half_height is tuned to fit one room. Adjacent DIM rooms
show up at the frame edges on their own, which is the continuous-dungeon read the
epic is after, without giving up the framing already tuned.

Picks confined to the current room are what hold the "visible is not addressable"
line from the epic's decision 8. Travel to a room two doors away is out of scope
and this is where that stays true rather than half-true.
acceptance_criteria:
- world_to_grid round-trips against grid_to_world for a room at a non-zero origin.
- A click on a DIM room's floor produces no intent and sends nothing.
- The door back is still clickable and still crosses.
- The camera follows the party in a room whose origin is not (0,0), with no
  clamp fighting the follow.
- Combat framing centres on the current room, not the entrance.
notes: Live after emberdelve-xgg.4: the current room now stands at its absolute origin, so World.world_to_grid (world.gd) — still origin-centred — mis-resolves every floor click in any room but the entrance. pick_at drops the click silently, _sync_tokens re-slides tokens on every scene change, and token.gd paths from the wrong square. The branch is playable in the crypt and not in the gallery until this lands. test_world_to_grid_still_inverts_the_current_room asserts the old origin-centred behaviour and needs replacing with a round-trip against a room at a non-zero origin.
close_reason: world_to_grid is room-aware and pick_at resolves the room a floor hit landed in; camera clamp and combat framing translate to the current room's origin. 232 godot tests green, server suite exit 0. Commit c01d33a.

title: Draw visited rooms at a DIM render level
description:
The visual half.

- Give the client one policy function returning a render level per room: BLACK
  (never seen), DIM (visited, not current), LIT (current). Everything else keys
  off that, so switching visited rooms from DIM to LIT is a one-line change.
- DIM builds with real materials and torch models but no OmniLight3D and no
  flames. Only the current room contributes lights.
- The origin table persists across a crossing. World stops clearing _origins and
  _sizes on a roomId change and stops re-centring the new room on the world
  origin; rooms sit where the server put them and the camera moves instead.
- Props get per-room holders. Today Props is flat and keyed by bare prop id, and
  _instance_prop silently returns early when the name is taken. Prop ids are only
  unique within a room (see PropRef): PropPlacer names every room's first pillar
  pillar-0, so drawing two generated rooms would silently drop props. Per-room
  holders fix that and give dimming a natural traversal.
- Room._build_walls' `get_parent() is World` special case goes: every room takes
  its registered origin, including the current one.
design:
DIM as "no lights" rather than "reduced-energy lights" or "tint override" keeps
MAX_TORCH_LIGHTS a per-room budget however large the dungeon gets — only the
current room ever adds lights. Reduced-energy torches would cost 10 omni lights
per visited room and hand the generator milestone a light-count problem on day
one.

Known and accepted: a DIM room's brightness drifts with the current room's
LightingPreset, because the WorldEnvironment ambient is global (TORCHLIT 1.1,
DIM 0.7, DARK 0.35). The crypt seen from the gallery reads darker than the
gallery seen from the crypt. If that reads badly in play, a per-room tint is the
second knob; the first knob is DIM -> LIT.

The prop-id collision is latent today — crypt and gallery ids happen to differ —
and is fixed here rather than deferred because this is the change that makes
multi-room prop rendering exist, and the failure mode is a prop that silently
does not appear. That is the project's characteristic silent failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- Crossing to the gallery leaves the crypt drawn at DIM with its props; the scene
  does not re-centre and no room is rebuilt at the world origin.
- Crossing back returns the crypt to LIT and the gallery to DIM, as left.
- A room never entered is still BLACK.
- Only the current room contributes OmniLight3D nodes; count asserted in a test.
- Two rooms carrying the same prop id both draw their prop.
- DIM -> LIT for visited rooms is a one-line change (demonstrated in the commit
  message or a comment naming the line).
close_reason: Render levels landed: Room.level_for is the one policy (LIT current / DIM visited / BLACK never entered), Room.build is the one build path for every room, the client's origin table is never cleared so crossing moves the camera rather than the dungeon, and props hang under Props/<room id> so two rooms sharing a prop id both draw. Godot suite 224 tests green; Java suite 297 green, untouched. Follow-ups filed: emberdelve-xgg.7 (wire Rooms.coveredWalls()), and emberdelve-xgg.5 now depends on this and must land before a non-entrance room is clickable.

title: Read the current room through Table.room() everywhere
description:
Mechanical churn to match the new wire shape. Around fourteen call sites read
room-level fields straight off Table.scene — width, height, floorType, wallType,
lighting, exits, props, roomId — across world.gd, room.gd, camera_rig.gd,
lighting.gd and table.gd. Those fields no longer live at the top level.

Add a Table.room() accessor returning the current room's RoomView, and a
Table.room_by_id() for the others. Convert the call sites. No behaviour change in
this task: the world still draws one lit room and the rest black, exactly as
today, just read through the new shape.

Kept separate from the visual work so that a regression here is obviously churn
and a regression there is obviously the feature.
design:
Table remains the single owner of game state (invariant #3, and CONTEXT.md's
"Table"). The accessor is what stops fourteen call sites each doing their own
lookup into rooms[] by roomId.

Table currently mutates scene["props"] on a PropRevealed diff. That write moves
to the current room's RoomView, which is correct because the diff channel is
current-room-scoped.
acceptance_criteria:
- No production .gd file reads width/height/floorType/wallType/lighting/exits/
  props directly off Table.scene.
- PropRevealed still lands on the current room's props.
- Both suites pass with no visible change to the running game.
close_reason: Table.room()/room_by_id() land; room.gd, camera_rig.gd, lighting.gd and world.gd read the current room through them instead of Table.scene's old flat fields. PropRevealed now writes to the current room's RoomView. Client test suite (scene_fixtures.gd helper + all fixture updates) converted to the new SceneState wire shape. Both suites green: 217/217 Godot GUT, server ./gradlew test.

title: SceneState describes every known room, not one
description:
SceneState carries one room at top level plus a neighbours list of bare outlines.
Reshape it so every room is described the same way:

  SceneState { roomId, rooms: List<RoomView>, entities, blocked, mode, combat }

RoomView { roomId, width, height, floorType, wallType, lighting, props, exits,
originX, originZ, visited }. roomId says which room the party is in; entities,
blocked, mode and combat stay session-level and stay scoped to that room.

GameEngine.scene() ships a RoomView for every room in Rooms that the party has
either visited or can see through an exit of the current room. A visited room
carries its visible props, dressed via room(roomId) and filtered by the
room-qualified revealedProps. An unvisited one carries geometry only and
visited=false.

Entities are NOT shipped for non-current rooms. entitiesHere() is unchanged.
design:
Forced by emberdelve-5sc. The shared-wall owner is decided by BFS distance from
the entrance, not by which room the party stands in, so the current room and a
non-current room have to go through the same wall-building code. Two wire shapes
means two code paths and the rule implemented twice — which is how you get a wall
right from one side and wrong from the other.

RoomView matches the EntityView / CombatView naming already in dm.model.

Entities excluded deliberately: a token in a non-current room is a creature the
player can see that the DM's prompt was never told about, which is spec section
8b's contradiction risk with a monster in it. Spec section 4b already keeps
entities in the fold where they were left; this only declines to draw them.

Diff is unchanged. Diff.PropRevealed carries no roomId and does not need one:
reveal_prop only ever offers the current room's hidden props, so the diff channel
stays current-room-scoped by convention. Worth stating rather than rediscovering.

No Event carries SceneState, so SCHEMA_VERSION does not bump and recordFixture is
not required.
acceptance_criteria:
- rooms[] contains the current room, every visited room, and every room visible
  through a current-room exit; nothing else.
- The current room appears in rooms[] in the same shape as every other room.
- A visited room's props include secrets revealed in THAT room and exclude
  secrets revealed elsewhere (PropRef is room-qualified).
- An unvisited room carries visited=false and no props.
- No non-current room carries entities.
- SCHEMA_VERSION unchanged; session-m3-traversal.jsonl replays with exit 0.
close_reason: SceneState reshaped to { roomId, rooms: List<RoomView>, entities, blocked, mode, combat }; GameEngine.scene() ships visited + exit-visible rooms uniformly. Java suite (299 tests) and Godot suite (217 tests) pass; session-m3-traversal.jsonl replays identical, exit 0.

title: Anchor every room's origin at the entrance, server-side
description:
RoomOutline.beside computes an offset relative to the room the party is standing
in. That works for one hop and cannot place a room two hops away: composing the
offsets is the client's problem today only because the client never has to.

Walk the exit graph from Rooms.first() breadth-first, composing beside() offsets,
and produce an absolute origin for every room in Rooms. The entrance sits at the
world origin and never moves. beside() itself is unchanged and stays the single
implementation of the door-alignment arithmetic.

Cycles: first path wins. A second path to an already-placed room is ignored, not
reconciled — reconciliation is real world-space packing and belongs to the
generator milestone (spec section 3, "world-space packing").
design:
Chosen over having the client accumulate C_abs = B_abs + offset. RoomOutline's
doc comment states the reason the arithmetic is server-side: "so there is one
implementation of the arithmetic and it can be tested without a renderer."
Client-side accumulation moves composition somewhere it can only be tested with a
renderer, and turns a cycle disagreement into an emergent client behaviour rather
than a defined server one.

A one-way exit already yields null from beside() and is filtered out; a room
reachable only through one is simply not placed and not drawn.
acceptance_criteria:
- A pure function maps Rooms to roomId -> origin, unit-tested with no renderer.
- Rooms.first() is at (0, 0).
- A three-room chain A-B-C places C correctly relative to A.
- A cycle A-B-C-A places every room once, deterministically, first path winning.
- crypt/gallery origins match what RoomOutlineTest already asserts for one hop.
close_reason: Added Rooms.origins(): BFS from first(), composing RoomOutline.beside offsets, into an unmodifiable roomId->RoomOrigin map. TDD'd in RoomsOriginsTest (single room, one-hop matching RoomOutlineTest, three-room chain composition, cycle first-path-wins, one-way-exit exclusion).

title: Visited rooms stay on the board
description:
Today the world shows one room at a time. Crossing a threshold re-centres the
scene on the room just entered and the room just left drops to a near-black
outline, so the dungeon reads as a series of boxes rather than one place.

This epic keeps every room the party has stood in drawn and legible, at a DIM
render level, in a single world frame anchored at the entrance. The party still
occupies exactly one room and can still only act in that room: what changes is
what is drawn, not what is addressable.

Scope is chaining crossings without the scene cutting. Clicking a door two rooms
away and walking there is NOT in scope — that needs multi-room routing the
server does not have and collides with the arrival-narration beat.
design:
Ten decisions, taken in a grilling session on 2026-09-06.

1. RENDER LEVEL. Three levels chosen by one policy function: BLACK (never seen),
   DIM (visited, not current), LIT (current). Making visited rooms LIT instead of
   DIM must stay a one-line change — it is the agreed fallback if DIM looks wrong
   in play.
2. DIM MEANS NO LIGHTS. Real materials, torch models placed, but no OmniLight3D
   and no flames. Only the current room contributes lights, so MAX_TORCH_LIGHTS
   stays a per-room budget however large the dungeon gets. Known consequence: a
   DIM room's brightness drifts with the current room's LightingPreset ambient
   (TORCHLIT 1.1 vs DIM 0.7). Accepted; a per-room tint is the second knob if it
   reads badly.
3. PAYLOAD IS GEOMETRY + PROPS. Visible props including secrets already revealed
   there. No entities — a creature the player can see but the DM was never told
   about is spec section 8b's contradiction problem in a new costume.
4. WORLD FRAME IS SERVER-OWNED, ANCHORED AT THE ENTRANCE. BFS from Rooms.first()
   composing RoomOutline.beside offsets; ship each known room's absolute origin.
   Cycles resolve first-path-wins. Chosen over client-side accumulation because
   RoomOutline's own rationale is that the arithmetic lives server-side "so there
   is one implementation and it can be tested without a renderer". Real
   world-space packing stays deferred to the generator milestone (spec section 3).
5. SHARED WALL OWNERSHIP. The plane is drawn once by whichever room is nearer the
   entrance in that BFS, ties broken by roomId. Omission is a 1D interval overlap
   on the shared plane, not a direction match. This replaces "the room the party
   is standing in owns the shared wall", which stops being a usable rule once more
   than one room is visible.
6. UNIFORM WIRE. SceneState becomes { roomId, rooms: List<RoomView>, entities,
   blocked, mode, combat }. Every room including the current one is a RoomView
   carrying origin, size, floorType, wallType, lighting, props, exits, visited.
   Forced by decision 5: the wall owner is decided by BFS distance, not by which
   room the party stands in, so current and non-current rooms must go through one
   code path or the rule gets implemented twice.
7. CAMERA. Clamp and combat framing translate to the current room's origin
   instead of Vector3.ZERO. Not the discovered bounding box — that would let the
   camera drift off the party and _combat_half_height is tuned to one room.
8. DM UNCHANGED. Prompt and ToolSchema stay scoped to the current room. The line
   is: visible is not addressable. This is what keeps out-of-scope travel out
   rather than half-in.
9. FIXTURES ARE SYNTHETIC. Rooms.of() three-room chains and a cycle in the suite;
   no third authored room in content/, so the AGENTS.md anti-goal is untouched.
10. DOCS. One ADR for decisions 4/5/8, written after the server half proves them
    rather than before. AGENTS.md's shared-wall line amended in the same commit
    that makes it false. CONTEXT.md gains "world frame" and "render level" and a
    corrected "scene state" entry, each with the code that introduces the term.

FREE, CONFIRMED: no Event carries SceneState, so SCHEMA_VERSION does not bump,
recordFixture is not needed, and session-m3-traversal.jsonl keeps replaying. Diff
is unchanged and stays current-room-scoped by convention.

RISK: the interval-overlap wall rule is the riskiest piece. It takes on exactly
the parity problem the current code deliberately dodged, and a wall right from
one side and wrong from the other is only visible from one camera corner. Build
it server-side and pure, prove it on the synthetic three-room chain, then wire
the client.
acceptance_criteria:
- Crossing from the crypt to the gallery leaves the crypt drawn, DIM, with its
  props and any secrets revealed there. The scene does not re-centre.
- Crossing back finds the gallery as it was left, and the crypt returns to LIT.
- No hole appears at the crypt's north corners when viewed from the gallery.
- A room never visited is still BLACK and still absent from the DM's prompt.
- Clicking anything in a DIM room does nothing and cannot issue a move.
- Both suites pass; session-m3-traversal.jsonl still replays with exit 0.

title: Props are not click targets yet
description: world.gd _target_under considers only wall segments carrying an exit_id. An earlier cut scanned Props as well, so that objects would be clickable generally, and it broke the door: picking takes the nearest hit, and brazier-east stood between the camera corner and the north wall. It won the ray, had no intent, and fell through to a null square. When a prop gains a real action (open the sarcophagus, search the alcove), add it to _target_under and decide how it ranks against a doorway and against the floor square behind it. test_overlay.gd's DOORWAY fixture now carries the crypt's real furniture, so a regression shows up.
notes:
Pulled into M4 (emberdelve-4h9) 2026-09-07. Two children hard-depend on it: 4h9.4 (the objective is a prop you take) and 4h9.6 (DM-placed markers). Section 2a of the design doc is the argument - an objective the player cannot pick up is not an objective, and routing 'take the relic' through free text alone puts a mechanical outcome back on the narrator's side of the governing principle.

---

**emberdelve-ffi.3 resolved 2026-09-10: the party's carried torch is never a pick target.**

The party carries a lit torch, with the mesh mounted on a `BoneAttachment3D` at the Knight's
`handslot.l`. **It must never enter `_target_under`,** and the reason is this ticket's own measured
lesson wearing a worse hat: `brazier-east` stood between the camera corner and the north wall, won the
ray, had no intent to offer, and fell through to a square that was `null` because the ray had already
left the room. A mesh at hand height on the party token is that object — in front of the camera, and
**moving every turn**.

`ADR-0011` says the same thing from the other side: drawing a thing grants no affordance over it.

**What replaces the click.** Spending a torch is the most consequential action in the delve and it
needs a reliable path, so it gets a **button on an exploration action bar**, not a pick target — see
`emberdelve-4h9.2`. That is deliberately the cheaper of the two fixes AGENTS.md would allow, and it is
named now so the session that hits this does not reach for the picker because the thing is right there
on screen.

This changes nothing about what this ticket has to do. It only closes one candidate.

comments.author: hampton.black
comments.text: emberdelve-xgg moves props into per-room holders (prop ids are only unique within a room). When this is picked up, _target_under must scan the current room's holder only — a prop in a DIM room must never win a ray, for the same reason a DIM floor square resolves to no intent.

title: A neighbour room's wall may overhang the shared plane
description: room.gd now has a neighbour omit the entire wall run its answering door is in, so the two rooms do not draw coincident geometry. When the neighbour is WIDER than the room the party is standing in, the part of its perimeter that overhangs the live room's wall is now missing too — its floor runs to an open edge there. Invisible today because a neighbour is painted near-black and the crypt (12) is wider than the gallery (10). Will show the moment the generator packs rooms of mixed sizes. Fix when it does: keep the overhanging segments and drop only the coincident run.
design:
Promoted from latent to live by emberdelve-xgg: the overhang is invisible only
while a non-current room is painted near-black. At the DIM render level it is two
1-unit holes at the crypt's north corners, visible from the gallery. Shipping
that would regress the playtest fix recorded in AGENTS.md — "a hole in the wall
is a way out, and there are no other holes".

The rule "the room the party is standing in owns the shared wall" is also no
longer usable. With several rooms visible at once a middle room has shared walls
on both sides, RoomOutline.back carries only one answering door, and two adjacent
DIM rooms would each omit their shared run and delete the wall between them.

REPLACEMENT RULE, two halves:

1. OWNERSHIP. The shared plane is drawn once, by whichever of the two rooms is
   nearer the entrance in the BFS from emberdelve-xgg.1, ties broken by roomId so
   it is stable and testable.
2. OMISSION. The non-owner omits only the segments the owner geometrically
   covers, computed as a 1D interval overlap on the shared plane using the
   absolute origins. Not a direction match — _on_a_shared_wall's whole-run
   omission is what loses the overhang.

Riskiest piece of the epic. It takes on precisely the parity problem the current
code dodged ("matching segment against segment can half-work when the rooms'
widths differ in parity"), and a wall correct from one side and wrong from the
other is only visible from one camera corner. Absolute server-computed origins
are what make it tractable: the comparison is on known world-space intervals
rather than grid indices of two differently-sized rooms.

Build and prove it server-side and pure, on the synthetic three-room chain,
before any client wiring.

AGENTS.md's shared-wall bullet is amended in the same commit as this change — it
is true until then, and false after.
acceptance_criteria:
- The shared plane between two rooms carries exactly one set of wall segments.
- Crypt (12) viewed from gallery (10): both overhanging north segments present,
  no hole at either corner.
- Two adjacent rooms that are both non-current still have their shared wall.
- A middle room in an A-B-C chain draws correct walls on both shared planes.
- Ownership is deterministic across runs and asserted without a renderer.
- AGENTS.md's "the room the party is standing in owns the shared wall" bullet is
  amended in this commit.
close_reason: Rooms.coveredWalls(): the shared plane is drawn once, by whichever room is fewer doors from the entrance (ties by roomId), and the loser omits only the segments the owner's run contains whole — a 1D interval overlap on absolute origins, not a direction match. Pure and server-side; client wiring is xgg.2/xgg.4. Five TDD'd cases in RoomsCoveredWallsTest, mutation-checked against reversed tiebreak, ignored hop distance, and whole-run omission. AGENTS.md's shared-wall bullet amended.

title: The gallery's cold brazier burns
description:
gallery.json's brazier-head is authored as 'a cold brazier ... choked with grey ash. Whatever burned here burned out a long time before the green fires downstairs were lit', and its overview says the same. But every BRAZIER prop instances godot/world/props/brazier.tscn, which has a lit OmniLight3D and glowing coals. So it has always burned (orange until emberdelve-4h9.16, green since), and since 4h9.16 it burns the exact colour the prose contrasts it with.

Another case of the board contradicting the DM. The fix is a lit/cold state the prop can carry, not a client-side special case on the id. It likely belongs with emberdelve-ffi.9's fires object (a room's fires moving to DARK has to put the braziers out too), or with emberdelve-4h9.7's appearance layer.

title: DM-placed markers - a fact you can click
description:
Section 9, Props are handles, not depictions: "If only rendered props are interactable,
the player learns to ignore everything the narrator improvises - which is the exact
opposite of what this game is for. The fix is the one assert_fact already uses: let the
model place a marker. It emits a position and a closed-enum tag, the engine drops a
generic interaction glyph there, and the scorched patch the prose just mentioned becomes
touchable. A fact you can click is a fact the board can back."

This is the partial answer to risk 3, the narrator describing a world change nothing can
back. It does not make the board agree with the hotdog. It does make the scorched patch,
the scratched sigil and the fresh tracks things the player can point at.

The tag is closed and validated like every other enum (invariant 7). The marker text is
a fact and makes one round trip back into the prompt, exactly as assert_fact already
does - no roll, no legal move, no renderer decision.

Reconcile-phase tool, not mechanics: the narrator is the one holding the information and
a false positive is a glyph nobody clicks. That is the rule from AGENTS.md, LLM tools,
applied straight.

Watch the interaction with anchors. emberdelve-pa8 records that assert_fact anchors
already drift, duplicate, and leak grid coordinates. A marker is an anchor that is now
visible, so pa8 stops being cosmetic the day this ships.
acceptance_criteria:
The DM can place a marker at a square with a closed-enum tag. It renders as a generic
glyph, is a pick target, and clicking it returns the fact to the DM as context. Grid
coordinates never reach narration. A test asserts an invalid tag or an out-of-bounds
square is rejected server-side.

title: assert_fact anchors drift, duplicate, and still leak grid coordinates
description:
Playtest 2026-09-07, both sessions. Four separate faults in what reaches ## Established.

WRONG ANCHOR, both sessions. Searching the goblin's body anchored to 'sarcophagus':
  s1 03:20:14 'The fighter's hurried hands found only sharp bits of scavenged iron... in the goblin's rags' -> on/sarcophagus
  s2 20:06:xx 'The sarcophagus lid has fresh scratches...' asserted after a turn about the goblin's body

NO DEDUP. Session 2 asserted the same sentence verbatim two turns apart with different anchors:
  19:59:5x 'Their fingers found no seam in the fluted pillars or the brazier's rusted joints.' -> at_square (5,0)
  20:00:3x the identical string -> ambient
WorldState.asserted (WorldState.java:233) appends unconditionally, so ## Established now carries it twice and the model is told twice that it is true.

RE-ASSERTING AUTHORED DRESSING. Session 2's last fact is crypt.json's propDescriptions.sarcophagus almost word for word. Nothing is learned and a slot in the per-room cap is spent.

GRID COORDINATES, still. at_square (0,6) in session 1, (5,0) in session 2. This is the m2-evaluation §8 finding recurring, and AGENTS.md already warns the coordinates will be read aloud the moment a writer is sloppier than Gemini.

The anchor is a closed enum and validated, so this is not an invariant-7 hole — it is the model choosing badly inside a legal set.
acceptance_criteria: A verbatim repeat of an existing fact in the same room does not create a second one. Consider whether an anchor pointing at a prop the turn never mentioned should be rejected rather than recorded.

title: A fact about one side of a door never reaches the other
description:
Playtest 2026-09-07, session 2. The player kicked door-north open in the crypt and the reconcile pass recorded it: 'The north door's mortise gave way and the slab door is now open.' From the gallery they asked what they could see back in the crypt, and the DM answered that the door 'sits shut against the mouth of the stair.'

WorldState.factsHere() is room-scoped, so the crypt's fact cannot reach the gallery. The gallery's prompt carried door-south's authored description, which said shut, with nothing contradicting it.

One door, two props, two descriptions, two truths. Same shape as the client bug already fixed on this branch — 'the thing you see and the thing you click are one object' — except the DM's view still has two of everything a doorway is. Exit carries the shared prop id and toRoomId, but there is no back-pointer to the answering exit; you resolve it by scanning the target room's exits for toRoomId == thisRoom.

emberdelve-xgg.10 removed the immediate trigger by taking 'shut' out of the gallery description and telling the model every exit is open. That makes this much harder to hit and does not fix it: any fact anchored on an exit prop still stops at the room boundary.

Options, none chosen: mirror an exit-anchored fact into the paired room at assert time; widen the prompt to include the neighbour's exit-anchored facts; or make the exit's state real, which is emberdelve-ql3 and makes this moot.

title: Give an exit a real shut/locked state
description:
Fix (b) to emberdelve-xgg.10's (a). That one made the prompt tell the truth: every exit is always passable. This one would make the fiction possible instead.

Today crossExit (GameEngine.java:284) refuses exactly one thing, leaving mid-fight. Exit is (id, x, y, direction, toRoomId) with no state.

Playtest 2026-09-07 wanted this twice without being offered it. Session 2 found a copper key on the goblin's body, tried it on the north door, and was told there was no keyway — because there is no lock in the model to put one in. Both sessions invented an ATHLETICS DC 20 to force a door that was never shut. The player is reaching for a mechanic that does not exist.

Weigh against AGENTS.md's anti-goals before starting: 'do not build a rules engine', 'do not generalize'. A locked door is arguably not a rule so much as the thing that makes two rooms a dungeon, but it is a new mechanical concept and it wants the content that justifies it. Likely belongs with the generator plan, not before it.

Sketch, not a design: Exit gains a closed state; crossExit refuses when shut and says so in its own words; something opens it (a check, a prop, a key as an item concept that does not exist yet). The client already ships SceneState.blocked for squares — an unusable exit wants the same treatment, decided server-side.
acceptance_criteria: Not ready to build. Decide first whether a locked exit belongs before the generator or with it.
notes:
PULLED INTO M4 2026-09-08. No blocking edge on purpose — the relationship with 4h9.8 runs the other
way and is conditional.

4h9.8 (author the site): "If a door in this site is meant to be shut, it needs emberdelve-ql3 behind
it. If it is not, its description must not say so." So authoring the site DECIDES whether this is
needed. A hard dependency would say the site cannot be authored until doors can lock, which is not
true and would make `bd ready` lie.

If 4h9.8 authors a shut door, close this first. If it authors none, this stays open past M4.

title: coveredWalls can name a room that is not on the wire
description:
GameEngine.coveredWallsOf() reads Rooms.coveredWalls(), which is computed over every room the entrance can reach. GameEngine.knownRoomIds() ships a subset — rooms the party has visited, plus rooms visible through one of the current room's exits. So a shipped room can be told to give up a segment to a room that is not on the wire at all, and the client draws a gap where nobody draws stone. A hole in a wall is a way out.

Unreachable in M3's two authored rooms, and unreachable in a chain too: a room is only shipped when it is visited or adjacent to the current room, and in both cases the room nearer the entrance is shipped as well. It stops being unreachable the moment the generator makes a dungeon with more than one path between rooms, because then the covering room need not be on any path the party has taken.

Found by the spec review of emberdelve-xgg.7.
design:
Two candidate fixes, neither obviously right yet:

1. Compute coveredWalls over the shipped set rather than every placed room. Correct by construction, but ownership then changes as rooms come into view, which is exactly the party-relative rule ADR-0010 threw out.
2. Ship the covering room whenever it covers something shipped. Keeps ownership stable, widens what the client is told exists — and RoomView already withholds an unvisited room's props, so a room drawn BLACK costs nothing but geometry.

Option 2 looks closer to ADR-0010's intent. Decide it against a real generated dungeon rather than on paper.
acceptance_criteria: A room shipped in SceneState.rooms is never told to give up a segment to a room absent from that list. Proven on a synthetic layout where the covering room is neither visited nor adjacent to the current room.
notes: ADR-0010 is the rule; ADR-0011 (visible is not addressable) is the constraint on widening what is shipped.

title: Give world.gd one room table instead of two parallel dictionaries
description:
_origins and _sizes in world.gd are two dictionaries keyed by the same room id,
and the world-frame work made them travel together everywhere: register_room()
writes both, grid_to_world and world_to_grid read both, _covers reads both
through _size_of, and room_at iterates _origins while resolving size through
_sizes. A small per-room value — origin and size together — wants to be born.

Replace the pair with one dictionary of a small typed inner class (GDScript has
no records; an inner class keeps it typed where a nested Dictionary would not).

Latent, not live. register_room is the only writer and writes both keys in the
same call, so the two cannot currently diverge. This removes a bug class, not a
bug — which is why it is P3 and why it should land AFTER the played verification
of emberdelve-xgg rather than before.
design:
THE TRAP, and the reason this is worth writing down rather than just doing.

The asymmetry is real: room_at iterates _origins, and the size it bounds-checks
against comes from _size_of, which FALLS BACK to the current room's dimensions
for an unknown id. So a room present in _origins and absent from _sizes would be
tested against the wrong rectangle and return a confident wrong answer — no
error, no empty result, just a click resolving to the wrong room. That is the
project's characteristic silent failure, and it is exactly the failure two
parallel dictionaries invite.

The wrong fix is to delete that fallback. It is deliberate and documented in
two places: _size_of and _covers both say why. A current room the server has
somehow not placed stays clickable at the origin, making the same guess
grid_to_world makes, because refusing it there would leave a room drawn on
screen with every click on it dropped without a word. grid_to_world and
world_to_grid have to make that guess identically or they stop being inverses.

So: one dictionary so the keys cannot diverge, fallback preserved exactly as it
is. The fallback stops being reachable-by-accident and stays reachable-by-design
for the unplaced-room case it exists for.

Sequencing: after emberdelve-xgg.7 and after the played verification. This
touches the placement and picking path, which is precisely what that session is
checking. Refactoring it first means two candidate causes for anything that
looks off in play, for no observable gain.

Source: code review of emberdelve-xgg.5, 2026-09-06.
acceptance_criteria:
- world.gd holds one room table, not two dictionaries keyed by room id.
- register_room's signature still takes size and origin together (its callers,
  including three in test_world.gd, are the check that they belong together).
- _size_of's fallback to the current room's dimensions is preserved, and
  grid_to_world / world_to_grid remain exact inverses under it.
- room_at no longer iterates one structure and resolves through another.
- godot suite green; no behaviour change in play.

title: Extract playtest findings from AGENTS.md into their own doc
description: AGENTS.md is 772 lines; its Voice section and subsections are 183 of them (Measured and worth keeping, Combat narration, The opening, Since fixed, Known unfixed, Carried out of M2, Carried out of M3). These are playtest findings, not rules — they are observations with dates, and they keep growing one milestone at a time. Moving them to docs/playtest-findings.md would cut AGENTS.md by roughly a quarter and give the findings somewhere to accumulate without diluting the rules. Needs a judgement call about which findings have hardened into rules and should stay behind.

title: Assess whether AGENTS.md can be stripped now that ADRs exist
description: AGENTS.md is 841 lines and is the operational document. With CONTEXT.md and seven ADRs in place, some of it is duplicated. Identify what genuinely moved versus what only looks duplicated, and cut only where the ADR is a strict superset.
close_reason: ADR-0003 amended with the gemini-3-8-flash/low switch; ADR-0008 added for the pick evidence; AGENTS.md model sections compressed 108 -> 39 lines with every fact preserved

title: Remove stale 'client' entry from .claude/launch.json
description: The 'client' configuration in .claude/launch.json runs 'npm run dev' in a cwd of 'client' on port 5173. That directory no longer exists — the Vite/Three.js client was replaced by Godot on 2026-08-23 (ADR-0006). The entry will fail if anyone selects it. Either delete it or replace it with a Godot launch entry.
close_reason: Deleted the client entry. The Vite/Three.js client it pointed at was replaced by Godot (ADR-0006); no Godot replacement entry was added because launch.json feeds the browser preview pane and Godot is a native desktop client with nothing to serve.
